narrative: On May 5, 2024, at approximately 11:39 PM, officers were dispatched to a reported burglary at a single-family residence located in the Parkview neighborhood of Westside. Upon arrival, officers observed signs of forced entry, noting that the dog door at the rear of the property had been forcibly enlarged to allow access. The victim reported that multiple rooms had been entered, with closet doors left open and personal items disturbed. Stolen property included various power tools, a flat-screen television, and a collection of rare coins, with an estimated total loss of $11,787. Officers canvassed the area and located a suspect matching the victim's description nearby. The suspect was detained and arrested without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Evidence, including latent fingerprints, shoe impressions, and surveillance footage from neighboring properties, was collected and secured for processing by the crime lab. The investigation is ongoing pending further forensic analysis.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Parkview neighborhood

narrative: On July 27, 2023, at approximately 10:24 AM, officers patrolling the Industrial Park neighborhood were flagged down by a concerned citizen in the 5200 block of Pine Avenue regarding a disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed an adult male suspect in the roadway, shouting obscenities and causing a disruption to nearby businesses and pedestrian traffic. Several witnesses reported that the suspect had been verbally aggressive and refused repeated requests to leave the area. Officers approached the suspect, who continued to exhibit disorderly behavior and ignored commands to cease shouting. After attempts to de-escalate proved unsuccessful, the suspect was placed under arrest for disorderly conduct without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers interviewed witnesses and documented statements. The investigation remains ongoing; individuals with further information are encouraged to contact the department. No property loss was reported.
address_block: the 5200 block of Pine Avenue

narrative: On July 15, 2023, at approximately 5:29 PM, officers responded to the intersection of Adams Street and Washington Avenue in the Lakefront neighborhood after being flagged down by a concerned citizen. The reporting party, identified as the victim, stated that unknown individual(s) had obtained their personal information without authorization and used it to open multiple fraudulent accounts, resulting in an estimated financial loss of $11,774. Officers conducted field interviews with two witnesses present at the scene, both of whom confirmed that the victim had recently received notifications of unauthorized transactions and accounts in their name. The victim provided documentation, including bank statements and account alerts, which were collected as evidence. No suspects were observed at the location, and the victim reported no physical injuries. Officers advised the victim on steps for identity protection and documented all witness statements. The investigation was closed due to lack of suspect information. No arrests were made.
address_block: the intersection of Adams Street and Washington Avenue

narrative: On July 14, 2023, at approximately 1643 hours, officers were flagged down by an employee at a retail store located in the 3200 block of Main Drive, Oak Park, regarding a report of identity theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the store manager, who reported that an unknown suspect had used fraudulent identification and credit information to make multiple large purchases totaling approximately $102,232 over the past week. The manager stated that the fraudulent transactions were discovered during a routine audit when discrepancies were noted in high-value electronics sales. Surveillance footage was reviewed, revealing the suspect to be an adult male, approximately 6’0” tall, medium build, wearing dark clothing and a baseball cap. The suspect’s identification documents have been collected as evidence. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers advised store personnel to preserve all related receipts and digital records. The investigation remains ongoing; anyone with information is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: a retail store in the 3200 block of Main Drive

narrative: On August 21, 2024, at approximately 9:27 AM, officers were flagged down by a resident in the 5100 block of Monroe Street, Greenfield neighborhood, regarding a reported weapons discharge. Upon arrival, officers canvassed the immediate area and spoke with multiple residents who stated they heard a loud noise resembling a firearm discharge but did not observe any individuals with weapons or any suspicious vehicles departing the area. Officers inspected the location for physical evidence, including spent shell casings or property damage, but none was found. No injuries were reported, and no witnesses could provide a suspect description. Officers checked nearby surveillance cameras; no relevant footage was available at this time. Based on the lack of evidence and witness accounts, the incident was determined to be unfounded. The case has been assigned to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the 5100 block of Monroe Street

narrative: On April 30, 2024, at approximately 2031 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported commercial burglary at a single-family residence located in the Downtown neighborhood of Oak Park. Upon arrival, officers observed the entry point was a dog door that had been forcibly enlarged, allowing unauthorized access. The residence displayed signs of a thorough search; multiple drawers and cabinets throughout the premises were found opened with contents strewn across floors. The victim reported the theft of several items, including power tools, a flat-screen television, and a collection of collectible coins, with an estimated total loss of $10,503. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two neighbors who reported seeing an unknown individual loitering near the property earlier in the evening; their statements were consistent regarding the suspect's clothing and approximate height. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers documented the scene with photographs and collected latent prints from the affected entry area. No arrests were made; the case remains open pending further investigation.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Downtown neighborhood

narrative: On October 8, 2024, at approximately 9:58 AM, officers responded to the 4600 block of Main Street in the North Hills neighborhood after being flagged down by a passerby reporting an aggravated assault. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult male, seated on the sidewalk, visibly distressed and holding his head. The victim exhibited a swollen nose, multiple facial contusions, and was bleeding from the nose and mouth. Officers rendered first aid while awaiting emergency medical services. The victim stated he was struck multiple times in the face with a metal pipe by the suspect, described as a male adult, following a verbal altercation. Witnesses in the area corroborated the account and provided video footage from a nearby business’s surveillance system. Officers canvassed the scene, locating the suspected weapon discarded in a trash bin. The suspect was located nearby, detained without incident, and cited for aggravated assault. The victim was subsequently transported to the hospital for further evaluation.
address_block: the 4600 block of Main Street

narrative: On April 23, 2023, at approximately 7:03 AM, officers were flagged down by a store employee outside a retail location in the 9600 block of Adams Drive, Highland neighborhood, regarding a weapons offense involving brandishing. The employee reported that a male suspect, described as mid-30s, approximately 5'9", medium build, wearing a dark jacket and blue jeans, entered the store and became agitated during a verbal dispute with another customer. The suspect reportedly displayed a metal object, later determined to be a large wrench, in a threatening manner while yelling at the customer. Officers located the suspect near the store exit, detained him without incident, and recovered the wrench from his possession. Witnesses provided corroborating statements, and security footage was collected as evidence. The suspect was cited for brandishing a weapon and released at the scene. No injuries were reported. The investigation is ongoing; anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: a retail store in the 9600 block of Adams Drive

narrative: On December 25, 2023, at approximately 12:55 PM, officers responded to a reported strong-arm robbery at a retail store located in the 6200 block of Adams Drive, within the Sunset Heights neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, later identified as a 38-year-old male store employee, with minor lacerations to his left forearm. The victim stated that a male suspect entered the store, approached the counter, and brandished a knife while demanding money from the register. The victim complied, handing over approximately $11,982 in cash. The suspect then fled the scene on foot. Officers canvassed the area and located a male matching the suspect description approximately two blocks away. After a brief foot pursuit, the suspect was apprehended without further incident. The knife was recovered from the suspect’s possession, and the stolen cash was located in a backpack carried by the suspect. Surveillance video was obtained from store management and will be retained as evidence. The victim was treated on scene by EMS for minor injuries. The suspect was transported to the station for booking.
address_block: a retail store in the 6200 block of Adams Drive

narrative: On January 29, 2023, at approximately 1500 hours, officers were dispatched to the 7-Eleven located in the Old Town Shopping Center in the Parkview neighborhood regarding a report of vandalism, specifically graffiti. Upon arrival, officers contacted the store manager who stated that sometime between 1400 and 1500 hours, an unknown suspect used spray paint to deface the north exterior wall of the business. The graffiti consisted of large, multi-colored lettering and symbols measuring approximately 8 feet by 4 feet. The store manager estimated the cost to remove and repaint the affected area at $1,251. Officers photographed the damage and canvassed the area for surveillance footage. No injuries were reported, and no suspect was observed on scene. The manager did not witness the incident but agreed to provide security footage to detectives. The case has been assigned for follow-up investigation. No arrests were made at the time of the report.
address_block: the 7-Eleven in the Old Town Shopping Center

narrative: On February 1, 2024, at approximately 7:22 AM, officers were dispatched to the auto parts store at 7400 Cedar Boulevard in the Harbor District regarding a report of a weapons offense involving brandishing. Upon arrival, officers contacted store employees who stated that a male suspect entered the premises, engaged in a verbal dispute with staff over a return, and subsequently displayed a handgun from his waistband without making direct threats. The suspect then exited the store and fled in a dark-colored sedan prior to police arrival. No injuries were reported and no property loss occurred. Officers obtained statements from three witnesses and secured surveillance footage from the store’s cameras for evidentiary review. The firearm was not recovered, and the suspect’s identity remains unknown at this time. The case was closed pending further investigative leads.
address_block: the auto parts store located at 7400 Cedar Boulevard

narrative: On June 13, 2024, at approximately 1833 hours, officers were flagged down by a store employee at the pawn shop located in the Eastgate Shopping Center, within the Sunset Heights neighborhood, regarding a report of disorderly conduct. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject inside the store, speaking loudly and gesturing with his arms. The store employee stated that the subject had been yelling and causing a disturbance after being told his merchandise could not be accepted for pawn. Officers made contact with the subject, who appeared agitated but was cooperative. The subject stated he was upset about the store’s policies but denied any threats or physical altercation. Witnesses in the store confirmed that no threats or physical contact occurred. Officers did not observe any evidence of injury, property damage, or weapons involved. After speaking with all parties, the subject agreed to leave the premises without further incident. No arrests were made. The disturbance was determined to be unfounded. No further action was taken at this time.
address_block: the pawn shop in the Eastgate Shopping Center

narrative: On March 8, 2024, at approximately 12:44 AM, officers were dispatched to a reported commercial burglary at an apartment complex located in the 6300 block of Adams Road in the Lakefront neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, the apartment tenant, who stated that upon returning home, they discovered the master bedroom had been disturbed. Officers observed that entry was gained through a dog door on the rear patio door, which appeared to have been forcibly enlarged to allow human access. The victim reported the theft of a laptop computer, a gaming console, and several bottles of prescription medication, with a total estimated value of $1,200. Officers conducted a canvass of the area and spoke with nearby residents, but no witnesses to the incident were identified. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The scene was processed for evidence, including the collection of possible fingerprint impressions from the dog door and bedroom surfaces. The suspect was located nearby, identified by officers, and subsequently cited for burglary. The case was assigned to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 6300 block of Adams Road

narrative: On August 19, 2023, at approximately 8:10 AM, officers responded to the intersection of Washington Street and River Avenue in the Sunset Heights neighborhood after being flagged down by a 60-year-old female victim. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim with minor abrasions to her left forearm and a distressed demeanor. The victim reported that while seated in her vehicle, a male subject approached from behind, displayed a black handgun, and demanded her wallet and phone. Fearing for her safety, the victim complied and exited the vehicle, at which point the suspect entered the driver’s seat and fled southbound on River Avenue in the victim’s gray sedan. The estimated loss included the vehicle, wallet, phone, and personal effects, totaling approximately $10,638. Officers conducted a canvass of the immediate area but did not locate additional witnesses or surveillance footage. The victim was provided medical attention on scene and gave a statement. The case remains open pending further investigation.
address_block: the intersection of Washington Street and River Avenue

narrative: On July 1, 2024, at approximately 03:35 hours, patrol units responded to a reported commercial burglary at a single-family residence operating as a business in the Riverside neighborhood of Eastgate. Upon arrival, officers observed an unlocked first-floor window with signs of recent entry. The interior inspection revealed multiple rooms had been searched, with closet doors left open and items displaced. The business owner reported the theft of computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $5,000, and various inventory items valued at $10,076 total. Officers canvassed the area and located a male suspect nearby matching witness descriptions; he was subsequently detained and arrested without incident. No injuries were reported. Witnesses interviewed on scene provided consistent accounts of seeing the suspect enter through the window and leave carrying bags. Officers collected fingerprint and surveillance evidence for further investigation.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Riverside neighborhood

narrative: On April 21, 2024, at approximately 0123 hours, officers responded to a reported domestic violence incident in the 5800 block of Adams Avenue, Midtown. Upon arrival, officers contacted the victim outside the residence, who exhibited visible bruising on both arms and the neck area. The victim stated that during a verbal argument, the suspect, identified as a known domestic partner, physically assaulted them and subsequently attempted to strike them with a vehicle before fleeing the scene in an unknown direction. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two neighbors who reported hearing a loud argument followed by screeching tires. Both witnesses observed the suspect driving a dark-colored sedan away from the location. Photographs were taken of the victim's injuries, and medical aid was offered but declined. Officers issued a broadcast for the suspect and the vehicle. Approximately 30 minutes later, the suspect was located nearby, detained without incident, and positively identified by the victim. The suspect was arrested for domestic violence assault and transported to the station for booking.
address_block: the 5800 block of Adams Avenue

narrative: On January 6, 2023, at approximately 0444 hours, officers responded to a vandalism call at Downtown Park near the intersection of Jefferson and Oak in the Downtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed multiple areas within the park, including the north-facing wall of the public restroom and several benches, defaced with spray-painted graffiti consisting of various symbols and lettering. No suspects were present at the scene. Park maintenance staff estimated the cost of repairs and removal at $7,302. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with a witness who reported hearing voices and seeing two unidentified individuals in dark clothing leaving the area at approximately 0430 hours. Surveillance footage from a nearby business was secured and is being reviewed for suspect identification. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers issued a citation for vandalism, pending further investigation.
address_block: Downtown Park near the intersection of Jefferson and Oak

narrative: On November 10, 2023, at approximately 1601 hours, officers were dispatched to the Target store at 1100 First Boulevard in the Millbrook neighborhood regarding a reported strong-arm robbery. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, a 42-year-old female employee, who sustained minor injuries to her left forearm. The victim stated that a male suspect entered the store and approached the customer service counter. The suspect displayed a knife, not a firearm, and demanded cash from the register. The victim complied, providing approximately $680 in cash. The suspect then fled the scene on foot in an unknown direction. Officers canvassed the area and obtained surveillance footage from store management. The victim was treated by EMS at the scene and declined further medical assistance. No arrests have been made at this time. The case was forwarded to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the Target store located at 1100 First Boulevard

narrative: On June 3, 2024, at approximately 2013 hours, officers responded to a reported vehicle burglary at an apartment complex in the 3500 block of Park Road, Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that upon returning to their parked vehicle, they observed the rear passenger door had been forcibly opened. Officers observed pry marks near the door handle and noted that the interior of the vehicle had been thoroughly ransacked, with glove compartment and center console drawers left open and personal items scattered throughout. The victim reported the theft of a laptop computer, a gaming console, and prescription medications, with an estimated total loss of $1,200. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with a witness who reported seeing an unknown male, approximately 5'10", wearing a dark hoodie and jeans, loitering near the vehicle around the time of the incident. Surveillance footage from the complex was collected for review. The suspect was located nearby, detained, and subsequently cited for vehicle burglary.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3500 block of Park Road

narrative: On June 29, 2023, at approximately 1300 hours, officers were flagged down by a concerned citizen in the 200 block of Valley Street, Cedar Grove, regarding a possible impaired driver. Upon arrival, officers observed a gray sedan parked at the curb with the engine running. Contact was made with the driver, described as an adult male, who exhibited slurred speech and bloodshot eyes. A strong odor of alcoholic beverage was detected emanating from the vehicle interior. The driver appeared disoriented and had difficulty locating and presenting his driver’s license and registration when requested. When asked to perform standardized field sobriety tests, the subject refused but consented to a preliminary breath test, resulting in a reading of 0.18% BAC. No weapons were present and no injuries were reported. The vehicle was secured and the driver released pending further investigation. Officers advised the subject of the ongoing investigation and provided contact information for witnesses to report any additional details.
address_block: the 200 block of Valley Street

narrative: On April 1, 2023, at approximately 2:17 PM, officers responded to a report of unlawful entry at the 7-Eleven located at 5500 Valley Boulevard in the Highland neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers contacted store employees who stated that an adult male, later identified as the suspect, entered the premises despite being previously advised by management not to return due to prior disturbances. The suspect was observed loitering near the beverage cooler and refused requests to leave. Officers located the suspect inside the store and detained him without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. A canvass of the surrounding area was conducted; however, no additional witnesses were located. The suspect was arrested on charges of trespassing and transported for booking. No property loss was reported, and store management provided a statement regarding the suspect’s prior exclusion from the premises.
address_block: the 7-Eleven located at 5500 Valley Boulevard

narrative: On June 5, 2024, at approximately 12:29 AM, officers were flagged down by an employee of the QuickMart convenience store located in the Parkview Shopping Center, Oak Park, regarding a reported petty theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that an unidentified individual had entered the store earlier and allegedly removed several items valued at a total of $4,099 without payment. The employee described the suspect as a male, approximately 5’10”, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. Officers conducted a canvass of the surrounding area, including adjacent businesses and parking lot, but no additional witnesses or relevant surveillance footage were located at that time. The reporting party was unable to provide further suspect information or a direction of travel. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Based on available evidence, the incident was determined to be unfounded at this time. No arrests were made.
address_block: the QuickMart convenience store in the Parkview Shopping Center

narrative: On March 4, 2023, at approximately 2:25 AM, officers were dispatched to the 9000 block of Lake Avenue in the University District regarding a suspected drug possession. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject, later identified as the suspect, standing near a parked vehicle. Officers noted the suspect appeared nervous and was attempting to conceal a small bag in his jacket pocket. A consensual search of the suspect was conducted, resulting in the recovery of a clear plastic bag containing a substance believed to be narcotics. Field testing later confirmed the substance as a controlled drug. Two witnesses at the scene provided statements, both reporting they observed the suspect handling the bag prior to officers’ arrival. The suspect was placed under arrest without incident and transported to the precinct for booking. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Evidence was logged and submitted for further analysis.
address_block: the 9000 block of Lake Avenue

narrative: On March 5, 2023, at approximately 1510 hours, officers were dispatched to the Wells Fargo bank at 9100 Maple Boulevard, Sunset Heights, regarding a reported DUI collision with injury. Upon arrival, officers observed a silver sedan with front-end damage parked in the bank lot. The driver, later identified as the subject, was seated in the driver’s seat exhibiting slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and confusion regarding their location and recent activities. The subject was unable to recall where they were coming from and admitted to consuming alcohol earlier in the day. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests, all of which the subject failed. A preliminary breath test indicated a BAC of 0.23%. One bank patron reported minor injuries after being struck by the subject’s vehicle while walking in the parking lot and was treated on scene by EMS. Surveillance footage from the bank was secured for evidence and is under review. No arrests were made, and the incident was determined to be unfounded after further investigation. Officers cleared the scene without further incident.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank located at 9100 Maple Boulevard

narrative: On February 20, 2024, at approximately 1512 hours, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 6500 block of Park Road, North Hills neighborhood, in response to a report of attempted auto theft. Upon arrival, officers met with a witness who stated that two unidentified subjects were observed in the parking lot attempting to push-start a vehicle, later identified as a late-model sedan valued at $23,815. The witness described the suspects as male, both wearing dark clothing, last seen driving away in the vehicle towards the east exit of the complex. Officers conducted a canvass of the area for additional witnesses and surveillance cameras. No injuries were reported and no weapons were observed. The vehicle owner was contacted and confirmed no permission was granted for use of the vehicle. Officers processed the scene, collecting latent fingerprints and possible DNA evidence from the vehicle’s door handles and steering wheel. All evidence was secured for analysis by the crime lab. No arrests were made; the case was closed pending further leads.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 6500 block of Park Road

narrative: On May 8, 2024, at approximately 1607 hours, patrol officers responded to a reported credit card fraud at the auto parts store located within the Cedar Grove Shopping Center, Industrial Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers met with the store manager, who stated that multiple unauthorized transactions totaling $94,293 had been processed over the past week using various credit cards. Store staff discovered the fraudulent activity during a routine account audit and identified several purchases of high-value auto parts by a male suspect, described as approximately 35-45 years old, medium build, wearing a gray hoodie and jeans. Surveillance footage was obtained and reviewed, showing the suspect conducting transactions at the register on several occasions. Officers canvassed the surrounding area for witnesses; however, no additional individuals with information were located. No injuries or weapons were involved. The case was closed after initial investigation due to insufficient evidence and lack of suspect identification.
address_block: the auto parts store in the Cedar Grove Shopping Center

narrative: On March 13, 2024, at approximately 0631 hours, officers responded to a reported burglary at an apartment complex located in the 5800 block of Oak Road in the Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers met with the apartment resident, who reported discovering a rear door forced open and multiple rooms disturbed. Officers observed closet doors and drawers open throughout the unit and signs of forced entry on the rear door frame. The victim stated that several items had been stolen, including computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $5,000 in cash, and various inventory items, with a total estimated loss of $9,796. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and collected surveillance footage from building cameras for review. Latent fingerprints and possible tool marks were documented and photographed. The investigation remains active and no arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 5800 block of Oak Road

narrative: On December 27, 2024, at approximately 1748 hours, officers were dispatched to Midtown Park near the intersection of Maple and Forest in the Millbrook neighborhood following a report of an attempted auto theft. Upon arrival, officers were flagged down by a witness who stated that two unidentified subjects were observed attempting to push-start a parked vehicle, described as a silver luxury sedan, before one subject entered the driver’s seat and drove the vehicle eastbound on Forest Street. The witness was able to provide a description of the suspects as two males, both wearing dark hooded sweatshirts and jeans. No injuries were reported and no weapons were observed during the incident. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspects or the vehicle. Park surveillance footage capturing the incident was secured for further review. The estimated loss reported by the vehicle owner was $57,263. Officers issued a citation for attempted auto theft and initiated follow-up investigation.
address_block: Midtown Park near the intersection of Maple and Forest

narrative: On September 13, 2024, at approximately 2011 hours, officers responded to South Valley Park near the intersection of Oak and Lake in the Millbrook neighborhood after being flagged down by a reporting party. The reporting party directed officers to the victim, who was visibly shaken and sustained minor injuries to the left forearm. The victim stated that while walking through the park, two unknown male subjects approached and blocked their path. One suspect displayed a blunt object, described as a metal pipe, while the other brandished a knife. The suspects demanded valuables, and the victim complied, surrendering a wallet, cellphone, and jewelry valued at approximately $13,790. After obtaining the items, the suspects fled southbound on foot. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspects. A metal pipe was recovered near the scene and secured as evidence. The victim was treated by paramedics on scene. No arrests were made at the time. The investigation remains ongoing pending further leads.
address_block: South Valley Park near the intersection of Oak and Lake

narrative: On November 7, 2024, at approximately 1545 hours, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 1800 block of Washington Road in the Midtown neighborhood regarding a reported weapons offense involving brandishing. Upon arrival, officers contacted the reporting party who stated that the suspect had threatened them by displaying what appeared to be a weapon. Officers conducted a thorough canvass of the area and spoke with residents in nearby units; no additional witnesses to the incident were identified. The suspect was located in the vicinity and detained without incident. A search of the suspect and immediate surroundings did not yield any weapons. The victim provided a statement describing the suspect's threatening behavior. No injuries were reported, and no property loss occurred. The suspect was arrested on scene for brandishing. Officers documented the incident and collected all relevant statements for further investigation.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 1800 block of Washington Road

narrative: On April 28, 2024, at approximately 11:49 AM, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 3600 block of Oak Drive, University District, regarding suspected drug paraphernalia found on the premises. Upon arrival, officers met with store management, who reported discovering a glass pipe with residue inside a restroom. Officers secured the item and documented its location. Several employees and a customer were interviewed, each stating they had observed an unknown individual enter and exit the restroom shortly before the paraphernalia was discovered; however, no clear suspect description was provided. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The paraphernalia was collected as evidence and logged for further analysis. The scene was cleared, and the case was closed due to lack of suspect information. No arrests were made, and no financial loss was reported.
address_block: a retail store in the 3600 block of Oak Drive

narrative: On May 19, 2024, at approximately 1518 hours, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 1800 block of Monroe Drive, University District, regarding a suspected DUI involving drugs. Upon arrival, officers observed the subject, an adult male, exiting a parked sedan in the store’s lot. The subject appeared unsteady on his feet and used the car door for support. Officers made contact and noted slurred speech and bloodshot eyes. The subject denied recent drug use and declined to participate in standardized field sobriety tests. He consented to a preliminary breath test, which yielded a result of 0.12% BAC. No illegal substances or paraphernalia were observed in the vehicle. The subject was cooperative and declined medical assistance. No injuries or property damage were reported, and no weapons were involved. Based on observations and test results, officers determined further investigation was warranted and referred the case to detectives for follow-up. No arrest was made at the scene.
address_block: a retail store in the 1800 block of Monroe Drive

narrative: On January 13, 2023, at approximately 8:23 AM, officers were flagged down by store management at the Walgreens pharmacy located in the South Valley Shopping Center, situated in the Industrial Park neighborhood, regarding a suspected check fraud. Upon arrival, officers spoke with the store manager, who reported that an unknown individual had presented a check in the amount of $14,306 for payment of pharmacy goods. Staff became suspicious after verifying the check with the issuing bank, which confirmed the check was fraudulent. The suspect, described as an adult male, approximately 35-40 years old, medium build, wearing a dark jacket and baseball cap, left the store prior to police arrival. No injuries or weapons were reported. Officers secured and reviewed surveillance footage from the pharmacy, which captured clear images of the suspect at the counter. A copy of the footage was collected as evidence. The case was documented and forwarded to the Fraud Unit for further investigation.
address_block: the Walgreens pharmacy in the South Valley Shopping Center

narrative: On February 16, 2024, at approximately 12:22 AM, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 7400 block of Main Road, South Valley neighborhood, for a reported domestic violence incident. Upon arrival, officers were met at the front entrance by the victim, an adult female, who displayed visible injuries including swelling and bruising to her face, as well as distinct bruises on her arms and neck. The victim stated that she had been assaulted by her cohabitating partner during a verbal argument that escalated inside their shared apartment. Officers observed disarray within the living area, consistent with a physical struggle. The victim reported that the suspect used a household object to strike her, although no weapons were recovered at the scene. Medical personnel were requested and treated the victim for minor injuries. A canvass of neighboring units was conducted; however, no additional witnesses were identified. The suspect was located inside the apartment, detained, and subsequently arrested for assault-domestic violence. The suspect was cited and transported for booking. Photographs of the victim’s injuries and the scene were taken.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 7400 block of Main Road

narrative: On March 16, 2023, at approximately 0034 hours, officers were flagged down by a security guard at Industrial Park Park, near the intersection of Adams Street and Valley Avenue in the Parkview neighborhood, regarding a reported grand theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that at approximately 0020 hours, an unknown suspect was observed removing several high-value electronic components from a secured storage area on the property. The suspect, described as a male adult wearing dark clothing and a gray hooded sweatshirt, left the scene on foot heading westbound on Valley Avenue. Officers canvassed the area and located the suspect matching the provided description attempting soplace stolen items into a parked vehicle. The suspect was detained without incident. A search of the vehicle recovered electronic equipment consistent with items reported stolen, with an estimated value of $13,285. Surveillance footage from on-site cameras was secured and logged as evidence. The suspect was arrested and transported to the station for booking. No injuries were reported.
address_block: Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Adams and Valley

narrative: On December 21, 2023, at approximately 1656 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Cedar Street and Forest Avenue in the Millbrook neighborhood in response to a report of suspected drug distribution activity. Upon arrival, officers observed a group of individuals congregating near the southeast corner but did not witness any active transactions. Officers approached and attempted to interview those present; however, all subjects denied involvement and refused to provide further information. A thorough canvass of the immediate area was conducted, including inquiries at nearby residences and businesses. No additional witnesses were identified, and no physical evidence of drug activity (such as narcotics, paraphernalia, or currency) was recovered at the scene. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were observed or mentioned. The incident was documented, and the scene was cleared without arrest.
address_block: the intersection of Cedar Street and Forest Avenue

narrative: On May 19, 2024, at approximately 1939 hours, patrol officers were dispatched to Riverside Park near the intersection of Elm and Jefferson in the Oak Park neighborhood regarding a report of vandalism (graffiti). Upon arrival, officers observed extensive spray-painted graffiti on the north-facing retaining wall adjacent to the main walking path. The affected area measured approximately 30 feet in length and 6 feet in height. The graffiti consisted of various stylized letters and symbols, some of which appeared gang-related. The suspect was advised of his rights and admitted to creating the graffiti, stating it was intended as "art." No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Photographs of the damage and recovered paint cans were collected as evidence. The suspect was cited for vandalism and placed under arrest. Video surveillance from the store was reviewed but did not show any unauthorized use or removal of the vehicle during the reported time. No physical evidence was recovered at the scene. narrative: On March 23, 2023, at approximately 10:34 AM, officers responded to a report of vehicle theft at the Bank of America branch located in the Midtown Shopping Center, Greenfield neighborhood. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; one bank employee recalled seeing an unfamiliar individual loitering near the vehicle but could not provide a detailed description. Surveillance video from the bank and shopping center was secured by officers for further review. Preliminary investigation suggested the theft may have involved a relay attack or electronic bypass, given the circumstances. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers did not observe any drugs in plain view and did not establish probable cause for a search. No arrests were made and no injuries were reported. Officers secured surveillance footage from a nearby business, which captured the incident. The footage is being reviewed for further investigative leads. The victim reported the theft of a laptop, gaming console, and prescription medications, with total estimated loss of $1,200. narrative: On April 6, 2023, at approximately 0257 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported burglary at a single-family residence located in the University District neighborhood near Downtown. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, the homeowner, who stated that upon returning home, they discovered the premises had been unlawfully entered. Officers observed that entry appeared to have been gained through a rear dog door, which had been forcibly enlarged to accommodate entry. A systematic search of the residence revealed multiple rooms in disarray, with closet doors throughout the home left ajar and contents disturbed. The victim reported several items missing, including various power tools, a flat-screen television, and a collection of rare coins, with a total estimated value of $8,559. The victim reported that several power tools, a 55-inch television, and a collection of rare coins were missing, with an estimated total value of $9,771. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the immediate area for witnesses; one neighbor reported seeing an unknown individual loitering near the property around 1730 hours but could provide only a vague description. No weapons were observed, and no injuries were reported. No evidence of criminal activity or property damage was found at the scene. The suspect then returned the firearm to his waistband before officers arrived. Officers located the suspect matching the provided description near a park bench and conducted a safety pat-down, locating a black semi-automatic handgun in his possession. The suspect was detained without incident and advised of his rights. Statements were obtained from the victim and a witness, both of whom corroborated the brandishing.
