Officers documented the graffiti with photographs, collected video surveillance from adjacent businesses, and completed a property damage report. At the conclusion of the investigation, no suspects were identified, and the case was closed pending further leads.
address_block: the public parking lot at 100 Third Way

narrative: On May 2, 2024, at approximately 0714 hours, officers responded to a reported weapons offense at the Home Depot located at 9600 Main Boulevard in the Industrial Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that an unidentified male suspect became agitated during a verbal dispute with an employee near the main entrance. The suspect retrieved a metal pipe from his vehicle and brandished it in a threatening manner, causing the employee to retreat and call 911. The suspect did not make physical contact with any individual and fled the scene in a dark-colored sedan prior to officers' arrival. Officers canvassed the area for surveillance footage and interviewed multiple witnesses, who corroborated the employee's account. A metal pipe, believed to be related to the incident, was recovered from a nearby parking space and submitted as evidence for processing by the crime lab. narrative: On October 12, 2023, at approximately 11:58 PM, patrol units were dispatched to the Home Depot at 5400 Pine Boulevard, Westside, following a reported grand theft. The suspect, described as a male wearing dark clothing and a baseball cap, was observed on surveillance video bypassing security measures and exiting through an emergency door without payment. No weapons were involved, and no injuries were reported. The estimated total loss was $4,643. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses but none were located. Video surveillance footage was obtained and logged as evidence. The scene was processed for fingerprints with negative results. The case remains under investigation. Anyone with information is urged to contact the department.

narrative: On April 12, 2024, at approximately 9:29 AM, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the Cedar Grove neighborhood of Old Town in response to a report of illegal weapons possession. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the resident, identified as the suspect, and advised them of the nature of the complaint. During the investigation, officers observed a prohibited weapon—specifically, a non-firearm device classified as "other" under local statutes—in plain view within the home. The suspect admitted to owning the weapon but stated they were unaware it was illegal. No injuries were reported at the scene. Officers conducted a canvass of the surrounding area and spoke with nearby residents, but no additional witnesses to the offense were located. The weapon was secured as evidence, and the suspect was taken into custody without incident. The estimated loss was $0. The case was documented for further review by investigators.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Cedar Grove neighborhood

narrative: On August 22, 2024, at approximately 1736 hours, officers were flagged down by the reporting party at an apartment complex in the 3700 block of Madison Road, located in the Downtown neighborhood, regarding a residential burglary. Upon arrival, officers observed that the garage door on the north side of the building had been forcibly pried open, with pry marks consistent with the use of a crowbar. Officers made entry and noted that only the master bedroom had been ransacked, with dresser drawers pulled out and items scattered on the floor. The victim, a resident, reported the theft of computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $500 in cash, and various inventory items, with an estimated total loss of $2,190. Officers conducted a canvass of the surrounding units and common areas but were unable to locate additional witnesses. No injuries were reported and there was no evidence of weapons used. Officers recovered latent fingerprints from the master bedroom doorframe and collected surveillance footage from building cameras. During the investigation, a male suspect matching the description provided by the victim was located nearby and detained. The suspect was positively identified by the victim and subsequently arrested without incident.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3700 block of Madison Road

narrative: On May 18, 2023, at approximately 1607 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported armed robbery at the public parking lot located at 6500 Maple Way, South Valley. Upon arrival, officers located the victim, a 39-year-old male, seated near his vehicle with visible abrasions to his right forearm and cheek. The victim reported that, while walking to his car, an unknown male suspect approached him from behind, produced a black handgun, and demanded his wallet and cell phone. Fearing for his safety, the victim complied, surrendering both items, which together contained approximately $8,331 in cash and valuables. The suspect then fled on foot toward the east side of the lot. Officers conducted an area search but were unable to locate the suspect. The victim described the suspect as a male, approximately 6'0", medium build, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. Paramedics treated the victim’s minor injuries at the scene. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and secured surveillance footage from nearby businesses, which is pending review. No arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: the public parking lot at 6500 Maple Way

narrative: On June 8, 2023, at approximately 11:33 AM, officers were dispatched to the 1100 block of Harbor Street in the Downtown neighborhood in response to a report of unlawful entry. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, a local business manager, who stated that an unknown individual had entered the premises without permission. The suspect was described as a male, approximately 35-45 years old, wearing a gray hoodie and dark pants. The manager reported that the suspect was observed walking through a restricted employee-only area before exiting the building when confronted. Officers conducted a search of the immediate area but were unable to locate the suspect. No physical damage or loss was reported, and no weapons or injuries were involved. Officers canvassed the area for potential witnesses and reviewed available security camera footage. The investigation remains open, and anyone with information is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: the 1100 block of Harbor Street

narrative: On February 22, 2023, at approximately 2035 hours, officers responded to a reported wire fraud at the Wells Fargo bank located at 1700 Third Boulevard in the Oak Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers met with bank staff who reported that a suspect, described as an adult male, had initiated a fraudulent wire transfer totaling $81,010 from a customer’s account. Bank staff provided transaction records and surveillance footage showing the suspect conducting the transaction at the teller window. The victim was identified as the account holder, who reported unauthorized activity after receiving a notification from the bank. Officers interviewed the victim and bank staff; no additional witnesses were identified during an area canvass. The suspect was located on scene, detained, and cited for wire fraud. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Evidence collected included transaction documents, surveillance video, and victim statements.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank located at 1700 Third Boulevard

narrative: On February 21, 2024, at approximately 11:43 PM, officers responded to a report of a simple assault at an apartment complex in the 8800 block of Lake Road, Greenfield neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult male, seated on the ground near the parking area, holding his head and displaying a bleeding laceration to his forehead. The victim stated that the suspect, known to him, intentionally struck him with a vehicle following a verbal altercation. Officers requested EMS, who transported the victim for medical treatment. The suspect was located on scene, detained, and subsequently arrested without incident. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; however, no additional witnesses were identified. Photographs of the victim’s injury and the suspect’s vehicle were taken as evidence. The suspect was transported to the station for booking. No property loss was reported. The investigation is ongoing.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 8800 block of Lake Road

narrative: On November 24, 2024, at approximately 8:01 AM, officers responded to a report of suspected drug possession at Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Lincoln and Elm in the Harbor District. Two witnesses who had contacted dispatch stated they observed the subject handling a small plastic bag containing a green, leafy substance believed to be marijuana. Officers approached the subject, identified him, and conducted a consensual search of his backpack, locating a plastic bag with approximately 5 grams of suspected marijuana. No weapons were found, and the subject denied intent to distribute, claiming personal use. Officers confirmed no injuries were reported. The subject was cited on scene for possession of a controlled substance and released. Photographs of the evidence were taken, and the suspected marijuana was placed into evidence. Witnesses provided written statements consistent with their initial accounts.
address_block: Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Lincoln and Elm

narrative: On March 28, 2023, at approximately 1942 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported aggravated assault at a single-family residence located in the North Hills neighborhood, South Valley. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult male, seated on the front lawn, holding his forehead and visibly distressed. The victim had a laceration approximately two inches in length above his right eyebrow, with moderate bleeding. Officers rendered initial medical aid and requested EMS, who later transported the victim for further evaluation. The victim stated that an unknown male suspect entered the residence, brandished a firearm, and struck him with the weapon during a verbal altercation. No shots were fired, and no property was reported stolen or damaged. A canvass of the area yielded no witnesses; however, officers recovered a metal object believed to be part of the firearm near the entryway. The crime lab was notified to process the evidence. Officers found no signs of forced entry and determined the report to be unfounded after further investigation. No arrests were made at the scene.

narrative: On August 26, 2024, at approximately 0730 hours, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence located in the Harbor District neighborhood, Downtown, in response to a reported noise complaint. Officers approached the residence and made contact with an adult occupant. The occupant acknowledged playing music but stated it was not intended to disturb neighbors. Officers advised the occupant of the complaint and explained relevant city ordinances regarding noise. The occupant agreed to lower the volume immediately. No signs of disturbance, weapons, or injuries were observed. No arrests were made. Officers cleared the scene at approximately 0745 hours. The situation was resolved on scene; no further action required at this time.

The witness observed the suspect walking among parked vehicles and attempting to open several car doors. Officers conducted a search of the area and located the suspect standing near a fenced section of the lot. The suspect was identified and detained without incident. He admitted to entering the area but claimed he was looking for a shortcut. No property loss or damage was reported, and no injuries occurred. Surveillance footage from nearby cameras was secured for evidence and will be reviewed to confirm the sequence of events. The suspect was cited for unlawful entry and released at the scene.
address_block: the public parking lot at 9900 Second Way

Officers made contact and performed a cursory search for officer safety, recovering a clear bag containing a green leafy substance consistent with marijuana. The subject denied ownership of the substance. Officers interviewed two witnesses on scene, both of whom reported observing the subject retrieve the bag from his backpack and attempt to hide it when police approached. The substance was seized as evidence. No arrests were made and no injuries were reported. The investigation remains open pending further analysis of the seized material.
address_block: the intersection of Oak Street and First Avenue

narrative: On March 29, 2023, at approximately 8:07 AM, officers responded to a report of criminal trespass at a single-family residence located in the Highland neighborhood of Old Town. The homeowner observed the suspect, described as a male approximately 30-40 years old wearing a gray hoodie and jeans, walking around the property before leaving through a side gate. No property was damaged and no items were reported missing. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two neighbors, both of whom confirmed seeing the individual on the property around the reported time. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers advised the homeowner on trespass prevention measures and completed a neighborhood check; the suspect was not located. The incident was documented and closed with no arrest.

narrative: On December 9, 2023, at approximately 2343 hours, patrol units responded to a report of shoplifting at the Walgreens pharmacy located at 5100 Forest Boulevard in the Lakefront neighborhood. The manager reported that the suspect exited the store without attempting to pay for the merchandise and left in an unknown direction. Video surveillance footage was reviewed and showed the suspect concealing items valued at approximately $6,723. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspect. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The investigation remains open. Witness statements and surveillance footage were collected for further review.
address_block: the Walgreens pharmacy located at 5100 Forest Boulevard

narrative: On September 10, 2024, at approximately 12:29 PM, officers were dispatched to the liquor store at 600 Hill Boulevard, Bayshore neighborhood, regarding a possible DUI. The driver exhibited slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and an odor of alcoholic beverage emanated from their breath. When asked, the driver was unable to state where they had come from. Officers requested the driver exit the vehicle and conducted standard field sobriety tests. The driver failed the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand tests. A preliminary breath test was administered, indicating a blood alcohol concentration of 0.13%. No injuries or weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses, but none were located. The driver was cited and taken into custody for DUI Alcohol. The vehicle was secured at the scene.

Officers collected digital evidence and secured surveillance footage from nearby businesses for further review. No suspects or witnesses were identified at the time of report. The case was forwarded to detectives for continued investigation. No arrests were made and no injuries were reported.
address_block: the public parking lot at 3900 First Way

Officers approached the suspect and issued verbal commands to cease the behavior, which were ignored. The suspect was subsequently detained without incident. No injuries or weapons were reported. address_block: a retail store in the 4900 block of Maple Drive

narrative: On February 21, 2023, at approximately 12:16 PM, officers responded to a report of vehicle vandalism in the public parking lot at 4500 Third Way, Millbrook neighborhood. No physical evidence, such as tools or items left at the scene, was recovered. The victim reported that the vehicle had been parked at the location since 10:00 AM and was undamaged at that time. Officers canvassed nearby businesses for potential witnesses but none were identified. No suspects were observed in the vicinity, and no injuries were reported. The incident was classified as unfounded pending further investigative leads.

The victim reported noticing an unknown individual in dark clothing loitering nearby prior to the theft but could not provide further description. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with two witnesses, neither of whom observed the theft but confirmed seeing a person matching the victim’s description in the vicinity. Evidence, including possible fingerprints from the vehicle and nearby surveillance footage, was collected and will be forwarded to the crime lab for analysis. narrative: On May 28, 2024, at approximately 1515 hours, officers responded to a reported carjacking in the public parking lot at 8700 Meadow Way, located in the Riverside neighborhood. The victim stated that while entering his vehicle, he was approached from behind by a male suspect, described as approximately 25-30 years old, medium build, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. The suspect reportedly displayed a black handgun and demanded the victim’s wallet and cellphone. Fearing for his safety, the victim complied. The suspect then ordered the victim out of the vehicle, entered the driver’s seat, and fled eastbound through the lot. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and located a bystander who observed a male subject running to the victim’s vehicle. Surveillance video from nearby businesses was secured for review. The victim valued the loss, including his vehicle, at approximately $5616. No arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: the public parking lot at 8700 Meadow Way

narrative: On August 21, 2024, at approximately 2:19 AM, officers were dispatched to a retail store in the 7900 block of Maple Drive, Highland neighborhood, following a report of a vehicle collision resulting in injury, possibly involving a DUI. Upon arrival, officers observed a sedan with front-end damage in the parking lot, and emergency medical personnel were attending to a passenger who reported minor abrasions. The driver, an adult male, exhibited slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and had difficulty producing his driver’s license upon request. A strong odor of alcohol was detected emanating from the vehicle and the driver’s breath. Officers administered standardized field sobriety tests, which the driver failed. A preliminary breath test indicated a BAC of 0.23%. Multiple witnesses stated the vehicle entered the lot erratically and struck a curb before coming to rest. No arrests were made as further investigation determined the incident did not meet DUI prosecution criteria, and the case was unfounded. Photographs of the scene and witness statements were collected.
address_block: a retail store in the 7900 block of Maple Drive

narrative: On August 6, 2023, at approximately 12:31 PM, officers were flagged down by a concerned citizen in Bayshore Park near the intersection of Monroe and Park in the Oak Park neighborhood. The reporting party indicated a male subject operating a grey sedan appeared intoxicated. Upon contact, officers observed the driver seated in the vehicle with the engine running. The subject exhibited slurred speech, bloodshot and watery eyes, and emitted a strong odor of alcoholic beverage. The driver was asked to exit the vehicle and demonstrated an unsteady gait while doing so. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests, including the Horizontal Gaze Nystagmus, Walk and Turn, and One Leg Stand, all of which the subject failed. A preliminary breath test was administered, yielding a blood alcohol concentration of 0.22%. Surveillance footage from nearby park cameras was secured for evidence and is under review. The subject was released at the scene due to no observed driving while officers were present, and arrangements were made for a sober party to retrieve the vehicle. No injuries or property loss were reported.
address_block: Bayshore Park near the intersection of Monroe and Park

Witnesses at the scene described a male suspect, approximately 25-30 years old, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans, seen striking the fixtures with a metal pipe. Officers located the suspect nearby, who was detained without incident. The suspect admitted to causing the damage following a verbal dispute with park staff earlier in the evening. Photographs of the damaged property and the metal pipe were collected as evidence, and the area was canvassed for additional surveillance footage. No injuries were reported. The suspect was arrested and transported for booking.
address_block: Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Monroe and Pine

narrative: On September 9, 2024, at approximately 7:25 AM, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 700 block of Oak Drive, Highland neighborhood, following a report from store management regarding suspected drug possession on the premises. The employee directed officers to the restroom, where officers observed a small clear plastic bag containing a white powdery substance, consistent with narcotics, on the counter. The substance was collected and logged into evidence. No injuries were reported, and no weapon was involved. Officers attempted to locate the suspect, described as a male, approximately 25-35 years old, wearing a black hoodie and jeans, but the individual had left prior to police arrival. The case remains open and has been assigned to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: a retail store in the 700 block of Oak Drive

narrative: On January 28, 2024, at approximately 3:05 AM, officers were dispatched to the Walmart parking lot at 7400 Oak Boulevard, Greenfield, regarding a reported motorcycle theft. Officers canvassed the area and obtained surveillance footage from Walmart security, which captured the suspect—a male, approximately 5'10", wearing a dark jacket and jeans—taking the motorcycle. Responding units located the suspect riding the stolen motorcycle approximately two blocks away and conducted a traffic stop. The suspect was taken into custody without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The stolen motorcycle, valued at $9,188, was recovered and returned to the victim. The incident was documented, and detectives were assigned for further investigation.

A search for the suspect yielded negative results. No shell casings or other physical evidence were recovered. Based on the investigation, the incident was classified as unfounded pending further leads.
address_block: the 500 block of Adams Avenue

narrative: On September 1, 2023, at approximately 1206 hours, officers were dispatched to 7900 Madison Boulevard, the local grocery store in the Old Town neighborhood, regarding a reported DUI with injury. Upon arrival, officers observed a midsize sedan partially parked across two spaces near the store entrance and a bystander rendering aid to an adult female who was seated on the curb, complaining of knee pain. The driver, later identified as the suspect, was still seated in the vehicle with the engine running. Officers noted a strong odor of an alcoholic beverage emanating from the vehicle interior and observed the suspect had bloodshot, watery eyes and slurred speech. The suspect exhibited difficulty locating and producing a driver's license when requested. The suspect refused standardized field sobriety tests but consented to a preliminary breath test, registering a BAC of 0.19%. Paramedics treated the injured party at the scene for minor injuries. Officers collected photographic evidence of the scene and secured the vehicle for processing. narrative: On February 8, 2023, at approximately 11:14 PM, officers were dispatched to the Starbucks coffee shop located in the Parkview Shopping Center, Downtown, in response to a reported motorcycle theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that he had parked his motorcycle directly in front of the establishment, left the keys in the ignition, and left the vehicle running while he briefly entered the store. Surveillance footage obtained from Starbucks showed an unidentified male suspect approaching the motorcycle, mounting it, and fleeing the scene northbound through the parking lot. Officers canvassed the area and located the suspect and motorcycle approximately two blocks away. The suspect was detained without incident and placed under arrest. The motorcycle, valued at $72,174, was recovered and returned to the victim. No injuries were reported. Officers photographed the scene and collected video evidence. Investigation remains ongoing; witnesses are encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: the Starbucks coffee shop in the Parkview Shopping Center

narrative: On May 4, 2023, at approximately 2209 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported commercial burglary at an apartment complex located in the 6400 block of Cedar Road in the Lakefront neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed that the garage door had been forcibly pried open, consistent with use of a crowbar or similar tool. Inside the premises, multiple rooms appeared to have been systematically searched, with closet doors left open and contents disturbed. The business owner reported the theft of several computer equipment items, a cash register containing approximately $500 in currency, and various inventory items, with an estimated total loss of $568. Officers conducted a canvass of the area and interviewed available witnesses, but no suspect was identified on scene. Photographs of the point of entry and disturbed areas were taken, and potential fingerprints and tool marks were collected for analysis by the crime lab. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The incident was later determined to be unfounded following further review.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 6400 block of Cedar Road

narrative: On June 12, 2024, at approximately 1619 hours, officers were dispatched to the Best Buy electronics store at 3900 First Boulevard in the Millbrook neighborhood for a report of a possible DUI. Upon arrival, officers located a gray sedan parked askew in a space near the store entrance. Contact was made with the driver, an adult male, who exhibited bloodshot, watery eyes and slurred speech. Officers detected a strong odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from the vehicle and the subject’s breath. The driver struggled to produce his driver’s license and registration, repeatedly fumbling and appearing disoriented. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests, all of which the driver failed. A preliminary breath test was administered, yielding a BAC of 0.11%. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The subject was not arrested at the scene due to medical clearance pending additional investigation. The case remains open and has been referred to detectives for follow-up.
address_block: the Best Buy electronics store located at 3900 First Boulevard

narrative: On June 13, 2023, at approximately 1830 hours, patrol units responded to a reported DUI with injury at the liquor store located in the Lakefront Shopping Center, Sunset Heights neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle partially blocking the store entrance and a female subject seated in the driver’s seat. Officers detected a strong odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from the vehicle interior. The driver exhibited slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and had difficulty locating and producing her driver’s license when requested. A male passenger was present and reported minor pain in his right arm, stating the vehicle had struck a parking barrier. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests; the driver failed the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand assessments. A preliminary breath test indicated a BAC of 0.09%. No visible injuries required medical transport. Officers secured the scene and documented the incident. No arrest was made at this time; case referred to detectives for follow-up.
address_block: the liquor store in the Lakefront Shopping Center

narrative: On July 1, 2024, at approximately 11:21 AM, officers were dispatched to the Bank of America branch at 4800 Oak Boulevard in the Harbor District in response to a report of unlawful entry. Upon arrival, officers spoke with bank staff, who stated that an unidentified adult male entered a secured employee-only area without authorization. Staff confronted the individual, who exited the restricted area and left the premises without incident prior to officer arrival. No injuries were reported, and no property loss was identified. Officers secured and began reviewing surveillance footage to identify the suspect. Witnesses described the individual as a male, approximately mid-30s, wearing a gray hoodie and jeans. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspect. No arrests were made, and the incident was closed pending further investigative leads.
address_block: the Bank of America branch located at 4800 Oak Boulevard

narrative: On April 20, 2023, at approximately 1:08 AM, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the Industrial Park neighborhood, South Valley, in response to a reported domestic violence incident. Upon arrival, officers observed several bystanders separating the victim, an adult female, and the suspect, an adult male. The victim stated that during a verbal argument, the suspect struck her in the jaw with a closed fist. Although no visible injuries were present, the victim complained of jaw pain and declined medical assistance. Officers canvassed the area and located home surveillance cameras; video footage capturing the altercation was secured for evidence. Statements were obtained from the victim, the suspect, and two witnesses who corroborated the victim’s account. Officers photographed the scene and collected additional physical evidence. The suspect was not present when officers completed their investigation; the case remains open pending further review and potential charges.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Industrial Park neighborhood

narrative: On May 20, 2023, at approximately 2:27 AM, patrol officers were dispatched to the public parking lot at 5500 First Way in the Midtown neighborhood in response to a reported shoplifting incident. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect in the process of loading multiple high-value electronic items into the trunk of a silver sedan. Officers made contact with the suspect, who was detained without incident. The victim, a store manager from a nearby electronics retailer, identified the recovered merchandise as property stolen from the store, with an estimated total value of $14,503. The victim stated the suspect had exited the store without attempting to pay for the items. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers conducted a canvass of the area but were unable to locate any additional witnesses. The suspect was placed under arrest for theft and transported for booking. All recovered property was logged as evidence.
address_block: the public parking lot at 5500 First Way

narrative: On April 18, 2024, at approximately 0532 hours, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the Parkview neighborhood of Bayshore regarding a report of an aggravated assault involving a knife. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult male, seated on the front walkway, holding his head and displaying visible facial injuries, including swelling and bleeding from the nose. Officers secured the scene and rendered first aid while awaiting EMS. The victim stated that the suspect, known to him, had confronted him inside the residence during a verbal argument, during which the suspect produced a kitchen knife and struck the victim in the face with the handle. The suspect was located inside the residence and detained without incident. A kitchen knife was recovered from the living room table and photographed as evidence. The victim was transported to Bayshore Medical Center for evaluation of a possible broken nose and facial contusions. The suspect was cited and taken into custody. Detectives were notified and assigned for follow-up investigation.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Parkview neighborhood

narrative: On August 9, 2024, at approximately 1:18 PM, officers responded to a reported burglary at the apartment complex office located in the 3300 block of Second Road, Parkview neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a shattered ground-floor window on the north side of the office with glass scattered inside, indicating forced entry. The office interior was in disarray, with file cabinets pried open and contents rummaged. The on-site property manager reported that several items were missing, including assorted power tools, a flat-screen television, and a collection of rare coins, with an estimated total value of $8,318. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and reviewed available surveillance footage. During the search, a suspect matching a witness description was located on the premises and detained without incident. The suspect was found in possession of several stolen items. No injuries were reported. Crime scene technicians processed the scene, collecting fingerprints and documenting evidence. Investigation is ongoing.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3300 block of Second Road

narrative: On September 15, 2023, at approximately 2:59 AM, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 6900 block of Madison Drive, Lakefront neighborhood, in response to a reported theft from a vehicle. Upon arrival, officers observed a silver sedan parked in the lot with its driver’s side window shattered. The victim reported that several electronic devices and merchandise, valued at approximately $11,487, were stolen from the vehicle. Officers interviewed two witnesses who stated they saw a male suspect, approximately 30 years old, wearing a dark hooded sweatshirt, break the window and remove items from the car before attempting to flee on foot. Officers canvassed the area and located the suspect nearby, carrying bags matching the stolen property description. The suspect was taken into custody without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The recovered property was inventoried and returned to the victim.
address_block: a retail store in the 6900 block of Madison Drive

narrative: On April 5, 2023, at approximately 12:15 PM, patrol officers responded to a report of unlawful entry at a retail store located in the 2600 block of Meadow Drive, Midtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with store management, who stated that an adult male suspect had entered the premises despite having been previously issued a trespass notice for the location. The suspect was observed by staff entering through the main entrance and walking toward the back of the store. Officers located the suspect near the storage area and detained him without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers reviewed store surveillance footage confirming the suspect’s entry in violation of the trespass order. The suspect was placed under arrest for trespassing and transported to the precinct for processing. Evidence, including surveillance video and witness statements, was collected and will be processed by the crime lab. No property loss was reported.
address_block: a retail store in the 2600 block of Meadow Drive

narrative: On May 8, 2024, at approximately 1:10 AM, officers were dispatched to the QuickMart convenience store at 1300 Third Boulevard in the Lakefront neighborhood in response to a reported noise complaint. Upon arrival, officers observed loud music emanating from the parking lot area, where a group of approximately six individuals had gathered near several parked vehicles. The store was open and no disruptive activity was observed inside. Officers made contact with the individuals present, who stated they were celebrating a birthday and had temporarily increased the volume of their car stereo. Store employees and two customers interviewed at the scene confirmed the source of the noise and reported no threats or disturbances beyond the music. Officers instructed the group to lower the volume, which they complied with immediately. No injuries, property damage, or weapons were involved. The situation was resolved on scene and officers cleared without further incident.
address_block: the QuickMart convenience store located at 1300 Third Boulevard

narrative: On June 21, 2023, at approximately 11:44 AM, officers were dispatched to the 3300 block of Lincoln Avenue in the Industrial Park neighborhood regarding a reported simple assault involving a blunt object. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim at the front entrance of the building. The victim displayed a visible laceration to the forehead and minor swelling to the left cheek. The victim stated that while inside the premises, a known individual struck them in the face with a metal pipe following a verbal altercation. Medical personnel were summoned, and the victim was treated on scene for non-life-threatening injuries. Officers located the suspect inside the building and placed them under arrest without incident. A metal pipe believed to be the weapon was recovered as evidence. Witnesses at the scene provided statements corroborating the victim’s account. The investigation remains active; additional information can be provided to the department.
address_block: the 3300 block of Lincoln Avenue

narrative: On April 26, 2024, at approximately 5:44 PM, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Adams Street and Hill Avenue, Lakefront neighborhood, regarding a reported auto theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that their vehicle, a late-model luxury sedan valued at approximately $62,946, had been parked at the location and was missing when they returned. The victim reported that a spare key had been concealed on the vehicle and believed it was used to facilitate the theft. Officers canvassed the area and located two witnesses who observed an unknown male subject, approximately 25-30 years old, entering the vehicle and driving away at a high rate of speed. Both witnesses provided consistent descriptions of the suspect and direction of travel. Officers issued a BOLO and, within one hour, located the stolen vehicle and detained a suspect matching the provided description. The suspect was arrested without incident. No injuries were reported. The vehicle was recovered, and no weapons were involved. The investigation is ongoing.
address_block: the intersection of Adams Street and Hill Avenue

narrative: On June 13, 2023, at approximately 0344 hours, patrol units responded to a reported vehicle burglary at an apartment complex located in the 7900 block of River Road, Bayshore neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a parked commercial vehicle with an enlarged dog door on the side panel, consistent with forced entry. The vehicle's interior had multiple drawers opened and contents strewn across the floor, indicating a thorough search. The business owner advised officers that computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $5,000 in currency, and various inventory items were stolen, with an estimated total loss of $7,505. Officers photographed the scene and collected latent fingerprints and possible trace evidence for processing by the crime lab. No suspects were located on scene, and no injuries were reported. Witness canvassing was conducted but yielded no leads. The business owner was provided a citation for the report and advised regarding follow-up procedures.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 7900 block of River Road

narrative: On July 13, 2023, at approximately 7:01 AM, officers were dispatched to a reported identity theft at a retail store located in the 9700 block of Second Drive, within the University District. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the store manager, who stated that an unknown individual had used fraudulent identification to attempt a purchase totaling $9,823. The store’s loss prevention staff discovered discrepancies in the identification during the transaction, prompting them to deny the sale and notify police. Officers reviewed available security footage, which showed a suspect described as a male, medium build, approximately 5’10”, wearing a dark jacket and baseball cap. A canvass of the surrounding area and inquiries with neighboring businesses yielded no additional witnesses. No physical evidence was recovered at the scene. The victim’s account information was documented. No injuries were reported and no arrest was made. The incident was determined to be unfounded after further investigation revealed no actual loss occurred.
address_block: a retail store in the 9700 block of Second Drive

narrative: On August 3, 2023, at approximately 6:22 AM, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 900 block of Oak Road, Riverside neighborhood, in response to a report of an attempted auto theft. Upon arrival, officers contacted the reporting witness, who stated that they observed two unidentified subjects attempting to push-start a vehicle in the parking lot. The witness described both subjects as adult males, wearing dark clothing, and noted that after several minutes of pushing, the subjects succeeded in starting the vehicle and drove away in an unknown direction. Officers conducted a canvass of the complex and surrounding area but were unable to locate additional witnesses or surveillance footage. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The estimated loss was $30,269. Based on available evidence and lack of corroborating information, the incident was determined to be unfounded. No arrests were made at this time.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 900 block of Oak Road

narrative: On April 19, 2024, at approximately 2116 hours, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot located at 8200 Elm Way in the Parkview neighborhood regarding a reported motorcycle theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that their motorcycle, a 2023 black sport model valued at approximately $64,678, had been stolen. The victim reported that they had briefly left the motorcycle unattended with the engine running and the keys in the ignition while entering a nearby business. When the victim returned approximately five minutes later, the motorcycle was no longer present. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and potential surveillance footage. A review of nearby security cameras was requested. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The victim provided a description of the vehicle and confirmed no suspects were observed. The case was referred to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the public parking lot at 8200 Elm Way

narrative: On April 17, 2023, at approximately 1:48 AM, officers were dispatched to the Shell gas station located within the Highland Shopping Center in the Millbrook neighborhood regarding a reported wire fraud incident. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, an employee of the gas station, who reported that a suspect had fraudulently initiated a wire transfer totaling $30,008 from the store’s account using falsified identification documents. The suspect, described as a male in his late 30s, was detained on scene. Witnesses, including two customers and a second employee, were interviewed separately and provided consistent statements indicating the suspect presented fraudulent paperwork and acted nervously during the transaction. Officers collected evidence including the wire transfer receipt, identification documents used, and surveillance footage. The suspect was issued a citation for wire fraud and was placed under arrest without incident. No injuries were reported.
address_block: the Shell gas station in the Highland Shopping Center

narrative: On November 25, 2023, at approximately 8:01 AM, officers on patrol in the Greenfield neighborhood were flagged down by a witness in the public parking lot at 3000 Main Way regarding a weapons offense involving brandishing. Upon arrival, officers observed the suspect, described as an adult male, standing near a parked vehicle and holding what appeared to be a metal pipe in a threatening manner toward another individual, identified as the victim. The victim stated the suspect had approached him during a dispute over a parking space and raised the pipe while making threatening remarks. Officers secured the scene, instructed the suspect to drop the object, and placed him under arrest without further incident. No injuries were reported. The metal pipe was collected as evidence. Witness statements were obtained, and the case was assigned to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the public parking lot at 3000 Main Way

narrative: On January 16, 2024, at approximately 12:39 AM, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence located in the Riverside neighborhood of the University District in response to a vandalism report involving graffiti. Upon arrival, officers observed multiple areas of spray-painted markings on the exterior walls and garage door of the residence. The homeowner reported discovering the damage shortly before placing the call and stated no suspects were seen in the area. Officers canvassed the vicinity but found no witnesses or surveillance cameras with a view of the affected property. No physical evidence, such as spray paint cans or suspect items, was recovered at the scene. The estimated cost to repair the damage was reported as $8,358. No injuries occurred, and no weapons were involved. At the time of the report, the investigation remained ongoing. Residents with information regarding the incident were advised to contact the department. No arrests were made.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Riverside neighborhood

narrative: On September 25, 2023, at approximately 12:00 AM, patrol officers responded to a report of vehicle vandalism at a single-family residence located in the Eastgate neighborhood of Bayshore. Upon arrival, officers observed a late-model sedan parked in the victim’s driveway with significant damage, including multiple shattered windows, deep scratches along the driver’s side, and a slashed set of tires. The victim stated the vehicle was intact at 10:30 PM and discovered the damage upon hearing loud noises outside. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two witnesses residing nearby, both of whom reported seeing an unidentified individual dressed in dark clothing fleeing the scene on foot shortly after the noises were heard. No surveillance cameras were present at the residence or on adjacent properties. Officers photographed the damage and collected physical evidence, including possible paint transfer. The estimated loss was $10,555. The investigation remains open pending further leads.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Eastgate neighborhood

narrative: On January 10, 2023, at approximately 10:54 PM, officers responded to a report of identity theft at a retail store located in the 9400 block of Adams Drive in the Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, store management reported that a suspect had used fraudulent identification and credit card information to purchase electronics and gift cards totaling approximately $8,015. Officers observed the suspect attempting to leave the premises and detained the individual without incident. The suspect was found in possession of multiple credit cards bearing other individuals’ names, as well as a fake driver’s license. Store surveillance footage captured the suspect conducting transactions at multiple registers. The victim whose identity was used was contacted by officers and confirmed they had not authorized any purchases. The suspect was arrested for identity theft and transported to the police station for booking. Detectives were assigned for further investigation, and the evidence was logged into property. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved.
address_block: a retail store in the 9400 block of Adams Drive

narrative: On March 26, 2023, at approximately 7:58 AM, officers were dispatched to a reported residential burglary at a single-family home located on the 200 block of River Street in the University District. Upon arrival, officers observed that the rear door of the residence had been forcibly opened, with visible damage to the door frame and lock. The victim stated that the burglary occurred sometime between midnight and 7:45 AM, when they discovered the break-in. Inside, officers noted multiple rooms had been ransacked, with drawers and cabinets left open and their contents strewn across the floors. The victim reported that power tools, a flat-screen television, and a collection of collectible coins, valued at approximately $1,200, were missing, contributing to a total estimated loss of $5,587. Officers processed the scene, photographing the point of entry and collecting latent fingerprints from the door and various surfaces. No suspects were observed at the scene, and no injuries were reported. The case remains closed pending further leads or evidence.
address_block: the 200 block of River Street

narrative: On February 22, 2024, at approximately 1710 hours, officers on patrol in the Riverside neighborhood were flagged down by a witness in front of the liquor store located within the Old Town Shopping Center. The witness reported observing two unknown subjects approach a parked vehicle in the lot. According to the witness, the subjects appeared to manually push-start the vehicle before gaining entry and subsequently driving away in an unknown direction. Officers made contact with the vehicle owner, who confirmed that the vehicle had been left locked and unattended while they were inside the store. The vehicle is described as a late-model sedan with an estimated value of $67,644. No weapons were observed, and no injuries were reported. Officers canvassed the area for additional witnesses and requested store management to provide surveillance footage. Video evidence was secured and is currently under review for suspect identification. The investigation remains open pending further leads.
address_block: the liquor store in the Old Town Shopping Center

narrative: On March 23, 2024, at approximately 2:29 PM, patrol officers responded to a reported burglary at a single-family residence operating as a commercial business in the Lakefront neighborhood of Highland. Upon arrival, officers observed a shattered window on the north side of the residence with glass debris scattered both inside and outside. Entry appeared to have been gained through this window. The interior of the residence was visibly ransacked; furniture in the living room was overturned, and multiple drawers and cabinets were open. The business owner stated that several items had been stolen, including multiple computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $500 in currency, and various inventory items, with estimated losses totaling $12,052. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; no immediate witnesses were located. Photographs of the scene and evidence were taken, and latent fingerprint processing was conducted on accessible surfaces. No injuries were reported, and no weapons appeared to be involved. The investigation remains open pending further leads.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Lakefront neighborhood

narrative: On October 23, 2024, at approximately 1825 hours, officers responded to a reported grand theft at the QuickMart convenience store located at 6500 Pine Boulevard in the Eastgate neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the store manager, who advised that an unknown suspect entered the store at approximately 1810 hours and proceeded directly to the electronics display. The suspect, described as a male, approximately 5’10” with a medium build, wearing a black hoodie and blue jeans, was observed on surveillance footage removing multiple high-value electronic devices from the secured case. The suspect concealed the items in a large black duffel bag and exited the store without making payment. The total loss was estimated at $5,818. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and possible video surveillance from neighboring businesses. No injuries were reported, and no weapon was observed. The scene was processed for evidence, and the case was forwarded to detectives for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the QuickMart convenience store located at 6500 Pine Boulevard

narrative: On January 7, 2023, at approximately 11:50 AM, officers responded to Cedar Grove Park near the intersection of Valley and Harbor in the University District regarding an armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers located the victim, a 31-year-old female, seated on a park bench and exhibiting minor abrasions to her left forearm. The victim reported that an unknown male subject, described as approximately 5’10”, medium build, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans, approached her from behind while she was on her phone. The suspect brandished a black handgun and demanded her wallet and phone. Fearing for her safety, the victim complied, surrendering a purse containing a wallet, cell phone, and personal items valued at $6,906. The suspect fled on foot toward Harbor Street. Officers canvassed the area for the suspect with negative results. Two witnesses in the vicinity corroborated the victim’s account, observing the suspect’s flight and providing similar descriptions. Officers photographed the scene, documented injuries, collected witness statements, and provided the victim with medical assistance. The case was closed with no arrest made.
address_block: Cedar Grove Park near the intersection of Valley and Harbor

narrative: On July 2, 2024, at approximately 0632 hours, officers responded to the 8900 block of Meadow Street in the University District after being flagged down by a group of bystanders regarding a simple assault. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim and suspect being physically separated by two adult witnesses. The victim stated that the suspect struck them in the jaw with an open hand following a verbal altercation near a parked vehicle. The victim reported pain to the jaw area but declined medical attention, and no visible injuries were noted by officers. The suspect remained on scene and was cooperative during questioning, denying physical contact and stating that the argument was verbal only. Officers canvassed the immediate area for additional witnesses or surveillance footage but were unable to locate further evidence. Both parties were advised of their rights and provided information on obtaining a restraining order. The case remains open pending further investigation, and no arrest was made at the time of the report.
address_block: the 8900 block of Meadow Street

narrative: On July 5, 2024, at approximately 1:49 PM, patrol officers responded to a reported unlawful entry at a retail store located in the 4500 block of Pine Drive, Parkview neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers met with store management who stated that an unknown individual entered the premises through a rear employee-only door without authorization. The subject, described as a male, mid-30s, approximately 5’10” with short dark hair, remained in restricted areas for several minutes before leaving through the same door. No items were reported missing and no injuries occurred. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspect. Store management provided surveillance footage, which was secured as evidence and is pending review for identification purposes. Officers advised staff on trespassing procedures and documented the incident for further investigation. The case remains open pending additional leads.
address_block: a retail store in the 4500 block of Pine Drive

narrative: On May 20, 2023, at approximately 1411 hours, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot at 1800 Jefferson Way in the Bayshore neighborhood in response to a reported noise disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed a male individual, later identified as the suspect, operating a portable speaker at a high volume, causing a disturbance to nearby businesses and patrons. Multiple witnesses at the scene confirmed that the loud music had persisted for over thirty minutes, disrupting normal activity. Officers made contact with the suspect and requested he lower the volume; however, the suspect refused and became verbally aggressive. After repeated warnings, the suspect continued to disregard officers’ instructions, resulting in his arrest for disturbing the peace. Officers collected the portable speaker as evidence, documented witness statements, and photographed the scene. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. All evidence was secured for processing by the crime lab.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1800 Jefferson Way

narrative: On August 14, 2024, at approximately 2:01 AM, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence located in the Lakefront neighborhood of the Harbor District in response to a reported motorcycle theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim outside the residence. The victim reported that a high-value motorcycle, estimated at $44,345, had been parked in the driveway with the keys left in the ignition and the engine running while unattended. The victim stated that upon returning to the driveway after approximately ten minutes, the motorcycle was missing and no suspects were observed in the area. Officers canvassed the immediate vicinity for potential witnesses and surveillance cameras but found no immediate leads. No injuries or weapons were reported. The victim provided a description of the motorcycle and confirmed no prior suspicious activity in the area. Officers entered the vehicle details into state and national databases. The investigation remains ongoing; any individuals with information are encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Lakefront neighborhood

narrative: On December 6, 2023, at approximately 9:21 AM, officers responded to a report of criminal trespass at University District Park near the intersection of Elm and Madison in the Millbrook neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the suspect, described as an adult male, standing inside a fenced area clearly marked with "No Trespassing" signage. Officers approached the suspect and identified themselves, requesting the suspect to provide identification. The suspect stated he was aware of the signage but entered the premises to "rest for a moment." Officers confirmed with park staff that the suspect did not have permission to be on the property. The suspect was taken into custody without incident, searched for weapons (none found), and cited for criminal trespass. No injuries were reported. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses but none were located. The suspect was released on a citation at the scene. No property damage or loss was reported.
address_block: University District Park near the intersection of Elm and Madison

narrative: On November 16, 2024, at approximately 0641 hours, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 3200 block of Lincoln Road, Millbrook neighborhood, following a report of a possible impaired driver. Upon arrival, officers observed a sedan parked partially askew in a designated spot. The driver, later identified as an adult male, exited the vehicle with noticeable difficulty, using the door for support and displaying an unsteady gait. Officers made contact and detected slurred speech and constricted pupils. The subject was asked to perform standardized field sobriety tests. He failed the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand tests, exhibiting lack of coordination and inability to follow instructions. A portable breath test was administered, yielding a BAC of 0.15%. Officers interviewed two witnesses who reported observing the subject driving erratically and stumbling upon arrival. No weapons or contraband were found, and no injuries were reported. The investigation is ongoing.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3200 block of Lincoln Road

narrative: On June 10, 2024, at approximately 6:25 AM, uniformed officers were dispatched to Bayshore Park near the intersection of Monroe and Harbor in the Greenfield neighborhood following a report of possible drug possession. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject seated on a park bench exhibiting suspicious behavior consistent with narcotics use. Officers approached and made contact, advising the individual of the reason for their presence. During the encounter, officers observed a small plastic bag containing a white powdery substance partially concealed beside the subject’s personal belongings. The subject denied ownership of the substance and declined to provide further statements. No weapons were found, and no injuries were reported. Officers collected the suspected narcotics as evidence, secured the scene, and documented the items for submission to the crime lab. The subject was identified and released pending further investigation. No arrest was made at the time.
address_block: Bayshore Park near the intersection of Monroe and Harbor

narrative: On August 18, 2023, at approximately 1957 hours, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot located at 8500 Meadow Way in the Cedar Grove neighborhood in response to a reported petty theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that while they were away from their parked vehicle, personal property valued at approximately $4,085 was removed from the vehicle without consent. The victim described observing a male suspect, late 20s, wearing a gray hoodie and black pants, leaving the scene carrying a duffel bag. Officers canvassed the area and located a subject matching the description nearby. The suspect was detained and admitted to taking items from the victim's vehicle. Stolen property was recovered and documented as evidence. No injuries occurred, and no weapons were involved. The suspect was placed under arrest and transported for booking. The investigation remains ongoing, and witnesses are encouraged to contact the department with additional information.
address_block: the public parking lot at 8500 Meadow Way

narrative: On February 28, 2023, at approximately 5:15 AM, officers were dispatched to a reported domestic violence incident at a residence on the 7200 block of Main Avenue in the Midtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim and the suspect being physically separated by two adult bystanders. The victim, an adult female, appeared visibly upset and reported that the suspect, an adult male household member, struck her in the jaw with a wooden household object during an argument. No visible injuries were present at the scene; however, the victim complained of pain to her jaw and declined medical attention. Officers secured the scene and conducted separate interviews with both parties and witnesses. The suspect denied involvement, stating the altercation was verbal only.
