narrative: On October 16, 2024, at approximately 1632 hours, officers were dispatched to the Target store located at 7700 Pine Boulevard, South Valley, in reference to a reported credit card fraud. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the store manager, who stated that an unknown individual had attempted to make multiple high-value purchases totaling $90,317 using several credit cards that were later declined. The suspect, described as a male, approximately 5'10" with a medium build, wearing a black hoodie and jeans, left the store prior to officers’ arrival. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers obtained and secured surveillance footage showing the suspect at multiple registers. The store provided transaction records and declined receipts for evidence. After review, the investigation revealed no loss occurred as no purchases were completed. Officers advised store staff on fraud prevention measures and documented the incident as unfounded.
address_block: the Target store located at 7700 Pine Boulevard

narrative: On October 28, 2024, at approximately 4:43 AM, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 2400 block of Main Road, Midtown, in response to a report of a possible DUI involving alcohol. Upon arrival, officers located the subject seated in the driver’s seat of a parked vehicle. Officers observed the subject to have slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and an unsteady gait upon exiting the vehicle. The odor of alcoholic beverage was detected emanating from the subject’s breath. The subject declined to perform standardized field sobriety tests when requested. However, the subject consented to a preliminary breath test, which yielded a result of 0.12% BAC. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The subject was cooperative throughout the contact. No arrest was made at the scene pending further investigation. Officers advised the subject of the ongoing investigation and provided information for follow-up. No witnesses were present. Anyone with information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 2400 block of Main Road

narrative: On October 29, 2024, at approximately 7:59 PM, officers responded to a reported burglary at a business located in the 8600 block of Harbor Street, Downtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed that entry appeared to have been made through a dog door at the rear of the premises, which had been forcibly enlarged. Inside, the living room showed signs of ransacking, with furniture overturned and drawers pulled open. The business owner stated that several items were missing, including multiple pieces of computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $2,500 in cash, and various inventory items, with an estimated total loss of $12,205. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two witnesses, both of whom reported seeing an unknown individual near the rear entrance shortly before the incident but could not provide a detailed description. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers collected photographs of the scene and documented all evidence. The case was closed after initial investigation.
address_block: the 8600 block of Harbor Street

narrative: On May 30, 2024, at approximately 12:04 PM, officers were dispatched to Walmart located in the Sunset Heights Shopping Center, Industrial Park neighborhood, in response to a reported vandalism incident involving graffiti. Upon arrival, officers met with store management, who directed them to the eastern exterior wall of the building. Officers observed multiple large, spray-painted tags in various colors covering an area approximately 15 feet wide by 8 feet high. Store management stated the graffiti had appeared sometime between 8:30 AM and noon, and no suspects were observed. Surveillance footage was reviewed and provided to responding officers for further analysis. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The estimated cost of removal and repair was documented at $3,348. Officers photographed the scene and collected paint samples for evidence. The incident was forwarded to detectives for follow-up investigation; no arrests were made at the time of report.
address_block: the Walmart in the Sunset Heights Shopping Center

narrative: On February 7, 2024, at approximately 8:22 AM, officers were dispatched to the Bank of America branch located in the Downtown Shopping Center, Oak Park neighborhood, regarding a report of illegal weapons possession. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect inside the lobby, visibly concealing a prohibited weapon described as a collapsible baton in his jacket. Bank staff stated the suspect had entered the premises and appeared nervous, prompting employees to notify security, who then contacted police. Officers detained the suspect without incident; no injuries were reported. A search of the suspect’s person revealed the baton, which was seized as evidence. The suspect was advised of his rights and placed under arrest for illegal weapon possession. Witness statements were collected from bank staff and security. Surveillance footage was requested for review. No financial loss or further disturbance occurred. The investigation remains ongoing, and the department requests additional information from the public.
address_block: the Bank of America branch in the Downtown Shopping Center

narrative: On March 31, 2024, at approximately 5:32 AM, officers responded to a reported carjacking at a retail store located in the 8500 block of Washington Drive, Sunset Heights neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, a 31-year-old male, seated on the curb with visible abrasions to his left forearm and minor facial swelling. The victim reported that while he was entering his parked vehicle, an unknown male suspect approached from behind, produced a black handgun, and demanded the victim’s wallet and cellphone. The suspect then forcibly removed the victim from the vehicle and fled the scene in the victim’s red 2022 sedan. Officers canvassed the area and, based on witness descriptions and surveillance footage from the store, located the suspect and vehicle approximately three blocks away. The suspect was apprehended without further incident. Officers recovered the stolen items and the firearm used in the offense. The victim was treated on scene by EMS. All evidence was documented and secured.
address_block: a retail store in the 8500 block of Washington Drive

narrative: On December 5, 2024, at approximately 4:52 AM, officers responded to a burglary report at a residence located in the 8600 block of Elm Street, Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed signs of forced entry through an unlocked first-floor window, which was found partially open with dirt smudges on the sill. The victim reported that multiple rooms had been disturbed, with closet and cabinet doors left ajar and belongings displaced. Stolen items included assorted power tools, a flat-screen television, and several collectible coins, with a total estimated loss of $1,515. Officers conducted a canvas of the area and interviewed two neighbors who reported seeing an unknown individual wearing dark clothing in the vicinity between 4:30 and 5:00 AM. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers processed the scene for fingerprints and collected photographs of the entry point and disturbed rooms. The investigation remains open pending further leads.
address_block: the 8600 block of Elm Street

narrative: On January 16, 2024, at approximately 9:28 AM, officers were flagged down by a witness at the Shell gas station located at 5700 River Boulevard in the University District. Upon arrival, officers contacted the victim, who reported that while entering their vehicle, a male suspect approached the driver’s side door, produced a black handgun, and ordered the victim to exit the vehicle. The suspect forcibly removed the victim, causing minor injuries to the victim’s left arm, before entering the vehicle and fleeing eastbound on River Boulevard. The victim described the suspect as a male in dark clothing and a hooded jacket. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and secured surveillance footage from the gas station, which captured the incident. Emergency medical services assessed the victim at the scene. The estimated value of the vehicle and personal property taken was $10,960. The suspect was located a short distance away, detained, positively identified by the victim, and cited for robbery. Evidence, including video footage and witness statements, was collected for further investigation.
address_block: the Shell gas station located at 5700 River Boulevard

narrative: On February 3, 2023, at approximately 11:55 PM, officers on patrol in the Millbrook neighborhood were flagged down by a store employee regarding a criminal trespass at a retail store located in the 6000 block of Lincoln Drive. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that an individual previously issued a trespass notice had entered the store despite being advised not to return. The suspect, described as an adult male wearing a dark jacket and jeans, was located inside the premises near the front entrance. Officers identified the suspect and confirmed the prior trespass warning through store records. The suspect admitted to re-entering the store, stating he wanted to “look around.” No items were taken and no damage was reported. The suspect was cited for criminal trespass and released at the scene. No injuries or weapons were involved. Store management was advised of the citation. The investigation is ongoing; witnesses are encouraged to contact the department with information.
address_block: a retail store in the 6000 block of Lincoln Drive

narrative: On April 13, 2024, at approximately 12:33 PM, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Cedar Street and Park Avenue in the Bayshore neighborhood following a report of illegal weapon possession. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject standing near the southeast corner, matching the description provided by the caller. Officers conducted a safety pat-down and located a fixed-blade knife concealed inside the individual's jacket pocket. The subject was cooperative and provided verbal identification. No injuries were reported and no other individuals were present at the scene. Officers interviewed the reporting witness, who stated they observed the subject displaying the knife in a threatening manner earlier. The knife was collected as evidence and submitted for safekeeping. The investigation remains open; no arrest was made at this time pending further review. Anyone with additional information is requested to contact the department.
address_block: the intersection of Cedar Street and Park Avenue

narrative: On July 11, 2023, at approximately 0759 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Valley Street and Madison Avenue in the Westside neighborhood for a report of an armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers located the victim inside a nearby business, visibly shaken and with a minor laceration to the left forearm. The victim stated that while entering the driver’s seat of their vehicle parked on the southeast corner of the intersection, an unknown male suspect approached, brandished a black semi-automatic handgun, and ordered the victim to exit the vehicle and hand over personal belongings. The victim complied, surrendering a wallet, cellphone, and approximately $1,519 in cash. The suspect fled eastbound on Madison Avenue on foot. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and surveillance footage. The scene was processed and a wallet fragment, possible fingerprint evidence, and surveillance images were collected for further analysis. The investigation remains ongoing.
address_block: the intersection of Valley Street and Madison Avenue

narrative: On October 4, 2023, at approximately 1749 hours, officers were flagged down by a citizen on the 8300 block of Valley Avenue in the Harbor District regarding possible drug possession. Upon arrival, officers observed the suspect, an adult male, seated on a bus bench displaying nervous behavior. Officers approached and conducted a consensual interview. During the interaction, officers noted a strong odor of marijuana emanating from the suspect’s clothing. A subsequent search revealed a small plastic bag containing a substance believed to be methamphetamine concealed in his jacket pocket. The suspect was placed under arrest without incident. No injuries or weapons were reported. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses, but none were identified. The suspected narcotics were collected as evidence and submitted to the property room for analysis. The suspect was transported to the district station for processing.
address_block: the 8300 block of Valley Avenue

narrative: On November 19, 2023, at approximately 10:18 AM, officers responded to Millbrook Park near the intersection of River and Main in the Highland neighborhood after being flagged down by a passerby regarding an armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers observed a 48-year-old female victim near her parked vehicle, exhibiting minor abrasions to her left forearm and visibly distressed. The victim reported that while she was entering her vehicle, an unknown male suspect approached the driver’s door, brandished a knife, and demanded that she exit the vehicle and surrender her purse and cell phone. The victim complied, at which point the suspect fled on foot toward River Street with approximately $2,590 worth of personal property. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspect. Surveillance footage from nearby businesses was collected and is being reviewed. The victim was treated at the scene by paramedics. No arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: Millbrook Park near the intersection of River and Main

narrative: On March 10, 2023, at approximately 1828 hours, patrol officers responded to a reported armed robbery in the public parking lot at 1900 Monroe Way, located in the Oak Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult female, seated near her vehicle and visibly distressed, though she did not display any physical injuries. The victim reported that while walking to her car, she was approached from behind by a male suspect described as approximately 6'0", medium build, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. The suspect brandished a knife and demanded the victim's wallet and cell phone, stating, "Give me everything or I'll hurt you." The victim complied, and the suspect fled on foot toward Monroe Avenue. Officers conducted a canvass of the area but were unable to locate the suspect. No witnesses to the incident were identified. Evidence collected at the scene included security camera footage from nearby businesses and the victim’s statement. The estimated loss was $11,806. The incident was later determined to be unfounded pending further investigation.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1900 Monroe Way

narrative: On September 8, 2023, at approximately 1854 hours, officers responded to a reported vehicle vandalism at the Shell gas station located within the Greenfield Shopping Center, Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers met with the reporting party, the vehicle owner, who stated their white 2021 Mercedes-Benz SUV had sustained multiple deep scratches to the driver’s side doors and rear quarter panel while parked near pump #3. The estimated damage was reported to be $14,448. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two witnesses, both of whom stated they did not observe anyone tampering with or approaching the vehicle during the reported time frame. Review of on-site surveillance footage revealed no suspicious individuals or activity in the immediate vicinity of the vehicle. No evidence or graffiti tools were located at the scene. Based on the absence of corroborating evidence or suspect information, the incident was determined to be unfounded, and no arrests were made. The victim was advised of the findings and provided with a case reference.
address_block: the Shell gas station in the Greenfield Shopping Center

narrative: On April 21, 2023, at approximately 0308 hours, officers were flagged down by a male subject in the 400 block of First Avenue, Eastgate neighborhood, regarding an aggravated assault. Upon arrival, officers contacted the victim, an adult male, who displayed visible bruising on his arms and neck. The victim reported that an unknown male suspect confronted him outside a residence and, following a verbal altercation, produced a knife and threatened the victim before physically assaulting him. The suspect then fled the scene on foot in an unknown direction prior to officers’ arrival. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspect. The victim declined medical transport but was provided with information on victim services. Officers documented injuries and collected photographs as evidence. There were no witnesses present at the scene. The investigation is ongoing; anyone with information is encouraged to contact the police department.
address_block: the 400 block of First Avenue

narrative: On August 8, 2023, at approximately 6:53 AM, officers on patrol in the Harbor District were flagged down by a store employee at a retail establishment in the 9700 block of Maple Drive regarding suspected drug paraphernalia found on the premises. Upon arrival, officers spoke with the reporting party, who stated that while conducting routine cleaning near the rear entrance, they discovered a small plastic bag containing a glass pipe with apparent burn residue. Officers visually inspected the item and confirmed it appeared consistent with commonly used drug paraphernalia. No individuals were observed in the vicinity, and surveillance footage review was requested. The paraphernalia was photographed and collected as evidence in accordance with department procedures. No suspects were identified, no injuries were reported, and no arrests were made. The evidence will be forwarded to the crime lab for further analysis. The case was closed pending additional leads.
address_block: a retail store in the 9700 block of Maple Drive

narrative: On June 10, 2024, at approximately 5:04 AM, officers were dispatched to the Home Depot at 5400 Maple Boulevard, Millbrook neighborhood, in response to a report of unlawful entry. Upon arrival, officers made contact with store management, who stated that an individual had been observed entering the premises through an unsecured side door prior to business hours. Officers conducted a sweep of the building and located the suspect, described as an adult male wearing a dark jacket and jeans, near the lumber section. The suspect was detained for investigation. Surveillance footage was reviewed with management and indicated that the suspect entered the property at approximately 5:00 AM and did not attempt to remove any merchandise. The suspect stated he entered to seek shelter and had no intent to steal. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The suspect was issued a citation for trespassing and released at the scene. Surveillance footage was secured as evidence for further review.
address_block: the Home Depot located at 5400 Maple Boulevard

narrative: On February 9, 2023, at approximately 4:43 AM, officers were dispatched to a reported carjacking at the intersection of Forest Street and Adams Avenue in the Midtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who was located inside a nearby convenience store. The victim, adult male, stated he had parked his vehicle, a gray 2019 sedan, outside the establishment when an unknown suspect approached him as he exited the car. The suspect, described as a male, approximately 5’10” with a medium build, wearing dark clothing and a face covering, brandished a blunt metal object and demanded the car keys. When the victim hesitated, the suspect struck him in the left arm with the object, causing visible bruising. The victim complied and the suspect entered the vehicle, fleeing eastbound on Adams Avenue. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and surveillance video. The victim was treated by EMS on scene for minor injuries. Estimated loss is $10,287. The investigation remains ongoing.
address_block: the intersection of Forest Street and Adams Avenue

narrative: On December 28, 2024, at approximately 1400 hours, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex in the 3200 block of Valley Road, South Valley neighborhood, regarding a report of a subject brandishing a firearm. Upon arrival, officers contacted the reporting party, who stated they observed the suspect, described as an adult male, standing in the parking lot and displaying a black handgun in a threatening manner toward another resident during a verbal dispute. Officers located the suspect matching the provided description near the scene. The suspect was detained without incident and a black semi-automatic handgun was recovered from his waistband. Witnesses provided consistent statements regarding the suspect's actions. No injuries were reported. Officers collected the firearm and other physical evidence, which were logged for processing by the crime lab. The suspect was placed under arrest for brandishing a firearm.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3200 block of Valley Road

narrative: On 02/25/2023 at approximately 0628 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported armed robbery at the Walmart located at 2000 Valley Boulevard, in the Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed store employees and customers congregated near the front entrance and made contact with the victim, a cashier, who was visibly shaken but did not report any physical injuries. The victim stated that a male suspect entered the store, approached the checkout counter, and brandished a blunt object described as a metal pipe. The suspect demanded cash from the register, verbally threatening harm if the victim did not comply. Fearing for their safety, the victim provided approximately $11,497 in cash. The suspect then fled the scene on foot in an unknown direction. Officers canvassed the area and reviewed surveillance footage, which captured the suspect wearing dark clothing and a face covering. No arrests were made. The scene was processed for evidence, and witness statements were collected. Investigation determined the incident was unfounded.
address_block: the Walmart located at 2000 Valley Boulevard

narrative: On July 21, 2024, at approximately 1956 hours, officers responded to a reported armed robbery at Lakefront Park, near the intersection of Harbor and Monroe in the Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim standing near a parked vehicle, visibly shaken but physically unharmed. The victim stated that while entering their vehicle, an unknown suspect approached the driver's side door and verbally threatened them while gesturing as if armed, though no weapon was observed. The suspect ordered the victim out of the vehicle, then fled on foot towards Monroe Avenue with a backpack containing electronics and personal items valued at approximately $9,948. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and located one individual who reported seeing a person running from the scene, but was unable to provide a detailed description. Surveillance footage from nearby businesses was secured for review. No arrests were made at the time, and the incident was later determined to be unfounded after further investigation.
address_block: Lakefront Park near the intersection of Harbor and Monroe

narrative: On July 30, 2023, at approximately 5:38 PM, officers were dispatched to a residential burglary in the 8700 block of Pine Avenue, Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers observed the garage door showed signs of forced entry consistent with the use of a crowbar, with pry marks visible near the locking mechanism. The homeowner reported that only the master bedroom appeared disturbed. The victim stated that computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $8,500 in cash, and assorted inventory items were missing, with an estimated total loss of $8,085. Officers conducted a canvass of neighboring residences and spoke with available occupants; however, no witnesses to the incident or suspicious activity were identified. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers collected photographic evidence of the damaged garage door and processed the scene for latent fingerprints. The investigation remains closed pending further leads or identification of suspects.
address_block: the 8700 block of Pine Avenue

narrative: On June 2, 2023, at approximately 2301 hours, officers were flagged down by a concerned citizen near North Hills Park, at the intersection of Hill Street and Pine Avenue, within the Millbrook neighborhood. Officers observed a gray sedan parked partially on the curb with the engine running. Upon approach, officers noted the strong odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from the open driver’s side window. The driver, an adult male, displayed slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and was slow to respond to questions. When requested to provide a driver’s license, the subject fumbled through his wallet and struggled to locate the identification. Officers requested the subject perform standardized field sobriety tests, which he refused. The subject agreed to a preliminary breath test, yielding a result of 0.14% BAC. No injuries were observed or reported. A canvass of the park area was conducted, but no additional witnesses were identified. The subject was placed under arrest for DUI (drugs/alcohol), cited, and released per department policy. The vehicle was secured at the scene.
address_block: North Hills Park near the intersection of Hill and Pine

narrative: On July 23, 2023, at approximately 1851 hours, officers on routine patrol in the North Hills neighborhood were flagged down by a local business owner at the intersection of First Street and Madison Avenue. The reporting party stated that an unknown male adult had entered a fenced, posted area adjacent to the property without permission and refused to leave when asked. Upon arrival, officers observed the suspect, described as a male, approximately 40 years old, wearing a gray t-shirt and jeans, inside the restricted area. Officers made contact and issued multiple verbal commands for the suspect to exit, which he ignored. The suspect was subsequently detained without incident. The reporting party provided a statement confirming the lack of authorization for the suspect to be on the premises. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The suspect was placed under arrest for criminal trespass and transported to the station for booking. Detectives have been assigned for follow-up investigation.
address_block: the intersection of First Street and Madison Avenue

narrative: On February 19, 2023, at approximately 1547 hours, officers were flagged down by store employees regarding a theft that had just occurred at a retail store located in the 1500 block of Pine Drive, within the Eastgate neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers contacted the reporting party, who stated that a suspect had concealed multiple electronic items valued at approximately $3,679 and exited the store without attempting to pay. Store security detained the adult male suspect outside the entrance and recovered the merchandise, all of which was returned to the store. The suspect admitted to taking the items without payment. Officers conducted a canvass of the immediate area, but no additional witnesses were located. The suspect was issued a citation for petty theft per store policy and released at the scene. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers documented the incident, collected statements from the reporting party and suspect, and provided the store with a case information card.
address_block: a retail store in the 1500 block of Pine Drive

narrative: On November 22, 2024, at approximately 0016 hours, officers patrolling the Midtown neighborhood were flagged down by a witness near the intersection of Elm Street and Park Avenue regarding a reported weapons discharge. Upon arrival, officers observed no immediate signs of injury or property damage. The witness stated that moments earlier, an unknown suspect inside a dark-colored sedan had discharged a firearm into the air while stopped at the intersection, then fled eastbound on Park Avenue at a high rate of speed. Officers canvassed the area for shell casings and other evidence but found none. No victims or additional witnesses were located at the scene. Surveillance footage from nearby businesses is being sought for review. The incident remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact the police department. No arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: the intersection of Elm Street and Park Avenue

narrative: On June 16, 2024, at approximately 1922 hours, officers on patrol in the Sunset Heights neighborhood were flagged down by a witness near Highland Park, at the intersection of River Avenue and Harbor Street, regarding an attempted auto theft. The reporting party stated they observed two unknown subjects attempting to push-start a silver sedan parked along the curb. The witness described the subjects as adult males wearing dark clothing. After several attempts, the subjects succeeded in starting the vehicle and fled eastbound on Harbor Street. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the vehicle or suspects. Additional witnesses were interviewed at the scene and corroborated the initial account, noting no weapons were seen and no injuries occurred. Officers documented the scene and collected surveillance footage from nearby residences for further investigation. The estimated value of the stolen vehicle is $62,858. The investigation remains open.
address_block: Highland Park near the intersection of River and Harbor

narrative: On November 29, 2023, at approximately 2306 hours, patrol units responded to a reported auto theft at a single-family residence located in the Bayshore neighborhood of Eastgate. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that their vehicle, valued at an estimated $46,918, had been taken from the driveway. The victim reported that a spare key had been hidden on the exterior of the vehicle and believed it may have been discovered and used by an unknown suspect. Officers inspected the scene and found no signs of forced entry or broken glass. A canvass of the surrounding area was conducted; however, no witnesses or surveillance footage were identified. The victim provided a description of the vehicle and stated no one had permission to use it. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The investigation did not yield evidence supporting the theft, and the incident was classified as unfounded. No arrests were made at this time.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Bayshore neighborhood

narrative: On December 25, 2023, at approximately 1615 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Lincoln Street and Pine Avenue, Eastgate neighborhood, regarding a reported identity theft. Upon arrival, officers contacted the victim, who stated that their personal information had been used without consent to open multiple credit accounts, resulting in fraudulent purchases totaling approximately $8,439. The victim reported first noticing unauthorized account activity earlier that day, then arranged to meet officers at the incident location for safety. Officers identified a male suspect nearby matching the description provided by the victim. Upon investigation, the suspect was found in possession of forged identification documents and credit cards bearing the victim’s name. The suspect was detained and, after being advised of their rights, admitted to using the victim’s information to obtain goods. No injuries were reported. Officers collected the forged documents and credit cards as evidence, which were submitted for processing by the crime lab. The suspect was arrested and transported to the station for booking.
address_block: the intersection of Lincoln Street and Pine Avenue

narrative: On July 17, 2024, at approximately 5:18 PM, officers responded to a report of a vehicle collision with injury at Sunset Heights Park near the intersection of Lake and Oak in the South Valley neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a gray sedan stopped partially on the curb with visible front-end damage. The driver, later identified as the suspect, exhibited slurred speech and had difficulty locating their driver’s license and registration when requested. Officers noted a strong odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from the suspect and the interior of the vehicle. A passenger in the vehicle, identified as the victim, complained of neck pain and minor facial lacerations; medical personnel were summoned and provided on-scene care. Officers administered standardized field sobriety tests, all of which the suspect failed. A preliminary breath test indicated a blood alcohol content of 0.12%. The suspect was placed under arrest for DUI causing injury and cited accordingly. Photographs were taken of the scene, and statements were collected from the victim and a witness who observed the vehicle driving erratically prior to the collision. The case was forwarded to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: Sunset Heights Park near the intersection of Lake and Oak

narrative: On May 5, 2023, at approximately 12:06 PM, officers were dispatched to Harbor District Park near the intersection of Hill and Jefferson in the Sunset Heights neighborhood following a report of property destruction. Upon arrival, officers observed significant damage to park benches and a decorative fountain, with portions of the benches splintered and sections of the fountain chipped and defaced. Estimated loss was determined to be $1,159. Witnesses at the scene described a male suspect, approximately 20-30 years old, wearing a red jacket and jeans, seen striking the property with a metal rod. Officers located the suspect nearby, matching the provided description, and took him into custody without incident. The suspect was advised of his rights and declined to make a statement. No injuries were reported. Officers documented the damage, photographed evidence, and collected witness statements. The investigation is ongoing, and anyone with additional information is asked to contact the department.
address_block: Harbor District Park near the intersection of Hill and Jefferson

narrative: On April 12, 2024, at approximately 0315 hours, officers were dispatched to a report of domestic violence involving an assault with a knife at a residence on the 1100 block of First Street, Midtown. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim and the suspect being separated by two adult bystanders outside the residence. The victim, identified as an adult female, had a visible laceration to her forehead and was bleeding. Officers requested medical assistance, and paramedics arrived to provide treatment at the scene. The suspect, identified as an adult male, remained on scene and was detained for questioning. The victim stated that during a verbal argument, the suspect produced a kitchen knife and struck her, causing the injury. Officers recovered a knife from the kitchen consistent with the victim’s description. No additional witnesses were located during a canvass of neighboring units. The suspect was not arrested at the time pending further investigation. No property loss was reported. The incident was documented and referred to detectives for follow-up.
address_block: the 1100 block of First Street

narrative: On December 29, 2024, at approximately 7:26 PM, officers responded to a report of a possible DUI at Westside Park, near the intersection of Washington and Oak in the Cedar Grove neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle parked irregularly along the curb with its engine running. Contact was made with the driver, who exhibited signs of intoxication including slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and an odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from their person. The driver was unable to recall their recent whereabouts and appeared confused. Officers conducted standardized field sobriety tests; the driver failed the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand tests. A preliminary breath test revealed a blood alcohol concentration of 0.23%. No injuries or property damage were observed. The driver was not arrested at the scene, and the incident was documented for further investigation. Detectives have been assigned to follow up. No witnesses were present, and no weapons were involved.
address_block: Westside Park near the intersection of Washington and Oak

narrative: On September 4, 2023, at approximately 1747 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported vehicle theft at a retail store located in the 7100 block of Hill Drive, Bayshore neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that at approximately 1740 hours, a witness observed two subjects approach a parked motorcycle in the store’s lot. The witness reported seeing both subjects work together to push-start the motorcycle, after which one subject mounted the vehicle and drove it away, with the second subject leaving the scene on foot. The stolen motorcycle was described as a 2022 black and silver model, valued at approximately $69,925. Officers canvassed the immediate area for additional witnesses and surveillance footage but did not locate further witnesses. The victim was interviewed and provided documentation of ownership. A preliminary investigation led to the identification and citation of one suspect at a nearby location. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Photographs of the scene and statements were collected for evidence.
address_block: a retail store in the 7100 block of Hill Drive

narrative: On June 19, 2023, at approximately 2112 hours, officers were dispatched to the jewelry store at 8500 Third Boulevard, South Valley, regarding an attempted auto theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who reported that their vehicle, a 2021 luxury sedan valued at approximately $33,099, had been left unattended with the keys in the ignition and engine running while they briefly entered the store. The victim stated that upon exiting the store, they observed an unknown individual pulling on the driver’s door handle but fleeing on foot when confronted. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspect, described as a male wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. narrative: On April 8, 2023, at approximately 0834 hours, officers responded to a report of a domestic violence incident at the 200 block of Meadow Avenue in the Oak Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim and the suspect being physically separated by several bystanders near a parked vehicle. The victim, an adult female, had a visible laceration to her forehead and reported that the suspect, an adult male known to her, had intentionally struck her with a vehicle during a verbal altercation. Officers requested medical assistance, and the victim was treated on scene by paramedics for her injury. The suspect remained on scene and declined to provide a statement. Officers canvassed the immediate area for additional witnesses but none were located. The incident was documented, and photographs of the victim's injury and the involved vehicle were taken. The scene was processed for evidence. No arrests were made at the time; the investigation remains open.
address_block: the 200 block of Meadow Avenue

narrative: On July 30, 2024, at approximately 1944 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Adams Street and Hill Avenue in the Westside neighborhood in response to a reported motorcycle theft. Upon arrival, officers met with the victim, who stated that they had parked their motorcycle at the curb at approximately 1900 hours and secured it using the built-in locking system. The victim confirmed possession of both keys at the time of the incident and reported no signs of forced entry or broken locks. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with two nearby residents, neither of whom observed any suspicious activity during the relevant timeframe. No surveillance cameras were noted in the immediate vicinity. Based on the circumstances and lack of physical evidence, officers suspected a relay attack or electronic bypass was employed to steal the motorcycle. The estimated loss was valued at $51,188. The case was forwarded to the detective unit for further investigation. No arrests were made and no injuries were reported.
address_block: the intersection of Adams Street and Hill Avenue

narrative: On January 19, 2024, at approximately 5:42 PM, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 6500 block of Second Drive, Westside neighborhood, regarding a weapons offense involving brandishing of a knife. Upon arrival, officers made contact with store staff and witnesses, who reported that an unidentified adult male suspect entered the store, became verbally aggressive with an employee near the checkout area, and displayed a folding knife in a threatening manner. The suspect did not physically harm anyone and no injuries were reported. The suspect fled the scene on foot prior to police arrival. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspect. Surveillance footage was obtained and is being reviewed for suspect identification. Witness statements were documented and the knife was not recovered. No arrests were made. Estimated loss was $0 and the case was closed pending further investigative leads.
address_block: a retail store in the 6500 block of Second Drive

narrative: On April 2, 2024, at approximately 1954 hours, officers were dispatched to the Wells Fargo bank located within the Riverside Shopping Center in the Sunset Heights neighborhood regarding a report of suspected drug paraphernalia. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, a bank employee, who stated that while closing for the evening, they discovered a small clear plastic bag containing a glass pipe with residue, consistent with items commonly used for narcotics consumption, near the ATM vestibule. No persons were observed in the immediate area. Officers photographed the scene and collected the paraphernalia as evidence, tagging it for laboratory analysis. No suspects or witnesses were identified at the time. Officers canvassed the surrounding area and reviewed available exterior surveillance footage; however, no relevant activity was immediately observed. The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information regarding the incident is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank in the Riverside Shopping Center

narrative: On June 25, 2023, at approximately 1304 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported domestic violence incident at a residence in the 4400 block of Park Street, Cedar Grove neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult, seated on the front lawn, visibly distressed and holding their head. Officers noted fresh bruising on the victim’s right forearm and neck, as well as a small laceration to the scalp. The victim stated that a known household member struck them multiple times with a wooden object during a verbal altercation inside the home. Officers conducted a protective sweep of the residence but did not locate the suspect, who had reportedly fled prior to police arrival. Medical personnel were summoned and provided treatment to the victim at the scene. Officers photographed visible injuries and recovered a wooden broom handle believed to be the weapon used. The case remains open and has been referred to detectives for further investigation. No arrest was made at the time of the report.
address_block: the 4400 block of Park Street

narrative: On September 19, 2023, at approximately 7:18 AM, officers were dispatched to the McDonald's restaurant located in the South Valley Shopping Center, Old Town neighborhood, in response to a reported strong-arm robbery. Upon arrival, officers entered the premises and made contact with the victim, an adult male employee, who appeared visibly shaken and reported minor injuries to his left arm. The victim stated that while he was cleaning near the front counter, an unknown male suspect approached from behind, brandished a black handgun, and verbally demanded the victim's wallet and mobile phone. Fearing for his safety, the victim complied and surrendered the items, valued at approximately $8,718. The suspect then fled on foot toward the shopping center parking lot. Officers canvassed the area but were unable to locate the suspect. Surveillance footage was requested from store management. The victim declined medical transport. The case was determined to be unfounded following further investigation; no arrest was made.
address_block: the McDonald's restaurant in the South Valley Shopping Center

narrative: On October 11, 2023, at approximately 1:48 AM, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot at 6300 Maple Way in the Eastgate neighborhood in response to a report of a weapons offense involving brandishing. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that the suspect had approached them during a verbal altercation and threatened them by raising a metal pipe in a threatening manner. The suspect, located nearby, was detained without incident. A search of the area resulted in the recovery of a metal pipe consistent with the witness’s description. The victim and an additional witness provided written statements, corroborating the sequence of events. The suspect was cited for brandishing a weapon and released at the scene. No injuries were reported, and detectives were assigned to follow up on the incident.
address_block: the public parking lot at 6300 Maple Way

narrative: On July 27, 2024, at approximately 1421 hours, officers were flagged down by the resident of a single-family home in the North Hills neighborhood of Bayshore regarding a reported auto theft. The victim stated that their vehicle, a late-model SUV valued at $26,545, had been parked in the driveway and was locked at the time of the incident. The victim confirmed possession of both key fobs, indicating that the theft may have involved a relay attack or electronic bypass. Officers visually inspected the area for signs of forced entry or physical evidence but found none. A canvass of neighboring residences was conducted; however, no witnesses or surveillance footage relevant to the incident were identified. The victim reported no injuries and stated that no weapons were involved. Based on the lack of evidence and witness accounts, the incident was classified as unfounded at this time. No arrests were made, and further investigation is pending any additional information.
address_block: a single-family residence in the North Hills neighborhood

narrative: On December 13, 2023, at approximately 2:40 PM, officers responded to a reported vandalism incident at the Wells Fargo bank located at 9600 Adams Boulevard in the University District. Upon arrival, officers met with bank staff, who indicated that an unknown suspect had caused significant damage to the bank’s exterior windows and ATM kiosk. Staff reported hearing loud noises but did not observe the suspect. Officers conducted a thorough search of the area, but no suspect was located. Surveillance footage was reviewed and evidence, including broken glass fragments and possible tool marks, was collected for processing by the crime lab. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. The estimated property damage was $14,719. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with nearby business employees, but no witnesses were identified. After investigation, the incident was determined to be unfounded for criminal charges at this time, and no arrests were made.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank located at 9600 Adams Boulevard

narrative: On May 30, 2024, at approximately 11:25 AM, officers were flagged down by a park maintenance worker near the intersection of Pine and Meadow in the Industrial Park Park, Oak Park neighborhood, regarding a suspected criminal trespass. The worker reported observing an unknown individual inside a fenced-off maintenance area without authorization. Upon arrival, officers canvassed the area and did not locate any individuals matching the provided description. The maintenance worker stated that no property appeared damaged or missing, and no signs of forced entry were observed. Officers photographed the area and obtained a brief statement from the worker. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Based on the lack of evidence and absence of suspects, the incident was determined to be unfounded at this time. The investigation remains open pending additional information.
address_block: Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Pine and Meadow

narrative: On March 4, 2023, at approximately 2:29 AM, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Monroe Street and Adams Avenue in the Greenfield neighborhood for a reported armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers located the victim inside a nearby establishment, visibly shaken and with a minor laceration to the left forearm. The victim stated that while walking at the intersection, two suspects approached and used a dark-colored vehicle to block the path. One suspect, described as a male approximately 5’10”, wearing a black hoodie and jeans, brandished a knife and demanded all valuables. The second suspect assisted by searching the victim’s pockets. The suspects stole a wallet, mobile phone, and wristwatch, with a total estimated loss of $11,860, before fleeing in the vehicle eastbound on Adams Avenue. Officers secured the scene, canvassed for surveillance footage, and interviewed two witnesses who corroborated the victim’s account. EMS treated the victim on scene. The investigation remains open.
address_block: the intersection of Monroe Street and Adams Avenue

narrative: On August 10, 2023, at approximately 2310 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Second Street and Harbor Avenue in the Parkview neighborhood regarding a report of vandalism in progress. Upon arrival, officers observed fresh spray-painted graffiti covering the north-facing wall of a commercial building. The graffiti consisted of multiple large tags in red and black paint, extending approximately 30 feet in length. Officers made contact with three witnesses who reported seeing a male suspect, approximately 18-25 years old, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans, actively spray-painting the wall. The witnesses provided consistent descriptions of the suspect and stated he fled on foot eastbound on Harbor Avenue. Officers canvassed the area and located a subject matching the description nearby, holding several cans of spray paint. The suspect was detained and read Miranda rights. He admitted to painting the wall, stating it was an "art project." Officers photographed the damage and collected the spray paint cans as evidence. The property owner estimated the cost of repairs at $14,066. The suspect was cited and released at the scene. No injuries were reported.
address_block: the intersection of Second Street and Harbor Avenue

narrative: On July 27, 2024, at approximately 11:27 AM, officers responded to a reported petty theft at the public parking lot located at 800 Lincoln Way in the Parkview neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim standing near a parked vehicle and identified the suspect, a male adult, being detained by security personnel. The victim reported that personal electronics and accessories valued at $1,587 had been taken from the unlocked vehicle while it was unattended. Multiple witnesses in the vicinity stated they saw the suspect open the vehicle door and remove items before attempting to leave the area. Officers interviewed witnesses individually, who provided consistent descriptions of the suspect and the sequence of events. The stolen property was recovered from the suspect’s backpack. The suspect was placed under arrest without incident. No injuries were reported. Officers photographed the scene, collected statements, and logged the recovered property into evidence.
address_block: the public parking lot at 800 Lincoln Way

narrative: On January 18, 2024, at approximately 10:49 AM, officers were flagged down by a citizen in the public parking lot at 1400 Second Way, Oak Park neighborhood, regarding a suspected attempted auto theft. Upon arrival, officers observed a late-model sedan parked with the driver's side window shattered, and broken glass scattered on the ground adjacent to the vehicle. The vehicle’s ignition appeared tampered with. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed two witnesses, both of whom stated they observed an individual attempting to gain entry into the vehicle before being confronted by passersby. Officers located the suspect nearby, matching witness descriptions, and placed the individual under arrest without incident. The victim was notified and provided information regarding the estimated loss of $12,583. Photographs of the damage and glass evidence were collected. The suspect was transported for booking.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1400 Second Way

narrative: On May 16, 2023, at approximately 0446 hours, officers responded to a report of aggravated assault involving a vehicle at the 7700 block of Oak Avenue in the Bayshore neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult, seated on the sidewalk and holding their head. The victim stated that a known individual attempted to strike them with a moving vehicle following a verbal altercation, narrowly missing and causing the victim to fall to the ground. The victim reported pain to the jaw but declined medical transport; no visible injuries were noted at the scene. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and secured surveillance footage from a nearby business, which is pending review for evidentiary value. The suspect was not present upon officers’ arrival and has not been located. The victim was provided with further information on obtaining a restraining order. Case remains under investigation; no arrest made at this time.
address_block: the 7700 block of Oak Avenue

narrative: On February 7, 2024, at approximately 6:07 AM, officers were dispatched to Sunset Heights Park near the intersection of Hill and Park in the North Hills neighborhood regarding a reported strong-arm robbery. Upon arrival, officers located the victim, an adult male, inside a park shelter. The victim stated that while walking through the park, two individuals approached and blocked his path. One suspect, described as a male approximately 5’10” wearing a dark hoodie, brandished a knife and demanded the victim’s wallet, phone, and watch. The second suspect, also male, assisted by physically restraining the victim. The suspects took valuables estimated at $9,974 and fled on foot toward Park Avenue. The victim sustained minor injuries to his left arm and was treated on scene by EMS. Officers canvassed the area and detained two individuals matching the descriptions nearby. Both suspects were positively identified by the victim and placed under arrest. Evidence, including the knife and stolen property, was recovered. The investigation remains ongoing.
address_block: Sunset Heights Park near the intersection of Hill and Park

narrative: On November 25, 2024, at approximately 6:46 AM, officers responded to the 7600 block of Cedar Road in the Millbrook neighborhood after being flagged down by a resident outside an apartment complex. The resident reported suspected drug activity within the building. Upon arrival, officers made contact with an adult male subject in the common area who exhibited signs of nervousness. A consensual search of the subject’s backpack revealed multiple small plastic bags containing a substance believed to be methamphetamine. The subject was placed under arrest without incident. No injuries were reported and no weapons were located. Officers secured the suspected narcotics as evidence, photographed the scene, and transported the items to the crime lab for analysis. Witness statements were obtained from the reporting resident and another tenant who observed the suspect loitering prior to the officers’ arrival. The suspect was transported to the station for booking and further investigation.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 7600 block of Cedar Road

narrative: On 10/09/2024 at approximately 10:29 AM, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the South Valley neighborhood of Riverside in response to a reported battery. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult, seated on the front walkway holding their head and exhibiting visible facial injuries, including swelling and bleeding from the nose. The victim stated they had been struck in the face multiple times by a known individual during a verbal altercation inside the residence. No weapons were reportedly used in the assault. Officers observed blood droplets on the floor near the entryway and noted damage consistent with a physical struggle. Medical personnel arrived on scene and transported the victim to a local hospital for evaluation of a possible broken nose and facial contusions. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; a neighbor reported hearing shouting but did not observe the incident. Surveillance footage from a doorbell camera was collected for evidence. The suspect was not present upon officers’ arrival, and the case remains open pending further investigation.
address_block: a single-family residence in the South Valley neighborhood

narrative: On December 12, 2024, at approximately 2:26 AM, patrol units responded to a report of a weapons discharge at North Hills Park near the intersection of Jefferson and Lake in the Parkview neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect standing near a park bench, holding what appeared to be a flare gun. Witnesses in the vicinity stated they saw the suspect discharge the flare gun into the air moments prior to officers' arrival. Officers detained the suspect without incident and recovered the flare gun as evidence. A search of the immediate area revealed no injured parties or property damage. The suspect was advised of his rights and admitted to firing the flare gun, stating he was attempting to attract attention after an argument with a friend. The flare gun was collected and submitted to the crime lab for examination. Witness statements were recorded, and the suspect was transported to the county jail for booking on weapons offense charges. No injuries were reported.
address_block: North Hills Park near the intersection of Jefferson and Lake

narrative: On April 23, 2023, at approximately 2:16 AM, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 7000 block of First Drive, Downtown neighborhood, in response to a reported shoplifting incident. Upon arrival, officers made contact with store employees who stated that a suspect had allegedly removed merchandise valued at approximately $12,027 from the premises. Employees reported observing the suspect via surveillance cameras but were unable to provide a physical description, as the suspect’s face was obscured by a hooded garment. Officers canvassed the immediate area for witnesses; however, no individuals reported seeing anyone leave the store with stolen items. Officers reviewed security footage and collected digital evidence for further analysis. No forced entry was observed, and no injuries or weapons were reported. After a thorough investigation and review of available evidence, the incident was determined to be unfounded. No arrest was made at the scene.
address_block: a retail store in the 7000 block of First Drive

narrative: On July 26, 2023, at approximately 10:14 PM, officers responded to the liquor store at 900 Lincoln Boulevard in Greenfield after being flagged down by a witness reporting an armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, a 28-year-old female, standing beside her vehicle in the store parking lot. The victim had minor abrasions on her left forearm, which she stated occurred during the incident. According to the victim’s account, as she was entering her vehicle, an unknown male suspect approached the driver's side, brandished a knife, and demanded she exit the vehicle and surrender her purse. The victim complied, and the suspect fled on foot with her purse and store receipts, totaling an estimated loss of $5,424. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and collected video surveillance footage from the store. The victim was provided medical assistance at the scene. No arrests were made, and subsequent investigation determined the incident to be unfounded based on review of evidence and victim’s inconsistent statements.
address_block: the liquor store located at 900 Lincoln Boulevard

narrative: On November 15, 2023, at approximately 0514 hours, officers were flagged down by a witness at the intersection of Main Street and Hill Avenue in the Westside neighborhood regarding a disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject, later identified as the suspect, yelling loudly and using profane language in the roadway, causing a disruption to nearby residents and early morning vehicular traffic. Officers made contact with the suspect, who appeared agitated but was unarmed and did not make threats of violence. The suspect was verbally uncooperative but complied with officers’ directives to cease his behavior. Several bystanders reported that the suspect had been shouting for several minutes but had not engaged in any physical altercations or caused property damage. No injuries were reported. Officers remained on scene to monitor the situation until the suspect departed the area voluntarily. No arrests were made. The scene was cleared without further incident. Anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: the intersection of Main Street and Hill Avenue

narrative: On April 10, 2023, at approximately 9:59 PM, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex located in the 2400 block of Lake Road, Riverside neighborhood, in response to a report of possible drug distribution activity. Upon arrival, officers made contact with several residents who had witnessed what they believed to be suspicious behavior near the parking lot and common areas. Witnesses consistently described seeing individuals gathering briefly and exchanging small items, but none observed any clear evidence of drug transactions. Officers canvassed the area and conducted field interviews with the subjects present, who denied any involvement in illegal activity. No contraband or paraphernalia was located during a visual inspection of the premises, and no physical evidence was collected. Based on the lack of corroborative evidence and witness statements, the report was classified as unfounded. No arrests were made, and no injuries or weapons were reported.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 2400 block of Lake Road

narrative: On August 10, 2023, at approximately 6:18 AM, officers responded to a report of a vehicle collision with injury at University District Park, near the intersection of Hill and Monroe in the Riverside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a sedan stopped partially on the sidewalk. The driver, identified as an adult male, appeared unsteady and required the vehicle door for support while exiting. The driver exhibited slurred speech and had bloodshot eyes. Officers noted a strong odor of alcohol emanating from the subject. The driver refused to participate in standardized field sobriety tests but consented to a preliminary breath test, which registered a blood alcohol concentration of 0.17%. One passenger in the vehicle sustained minor abrasions and was treated at the scene by EMS. Witnesses present reported seeing the vehicle swerve before striking a curb. All witness statements were consistent with observed evidence. The driver was cited and placed under arrest for DUI with injury. No property damage was reported.
address_block: University District Park near the intersection of Hill and Monroe

narrative: On September 9, 2024, at approximately 1930 hours, officers responded to a reported grand theft at the public parking lot located at 100 Valley Way, in the Bayshore neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that while parked in the lot, an unknown male suspect forcibly removed a backpack containing personal electronics and cash valued at approximately $1,803 from the victim’s unlocked vehicle. The victim described the suspect as a male, late 20s, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. Witnesses in the area reported observing the suspect flee on foot toward Valley Way. Officers canvassed the immediate area and located the suspect matching the description hiding behind a dumpster. The suspect was detained without incident and positively identified by the victim. The stolen property was recovered in the suspect’s possession. The suspect was placed under arrest and transported to the station for booking. No injuries were reported. Investigation is ongoing.
address_block: the public parking lot at 100 Valley Way

narrative: On November 29, 2023, at approximately 1652 hours, officers were dispatched to the pawn shop located within the Riverside Shopping Center in the North Hills neighborhood in response to a report of a possible DUI. Upon arrival, officers observed a silver sedan parked askew in front of the business. Contact was made with the driver, an adult male, seated in the driver’s seat. Officers immediately detected a strong odor of alcoholic beverage emanating from the vehicle and noted the driver’s slurred speech and bloodshot, watery eyes. When asked for his driver’s license, the subject fumbled and struggled to locate it, displaying poor motor coordination. The subject declined to perform standardized field sobriety tests but consented to a preliminary breath test, which resulted in a blood alcohol concentration of 0.22%. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers collected the PBT device printout and documented the subject's statements. The evidence will be forwarded to the crime lab for further analysis. The investigation remains open.
address_block: the pawn shop in the Riverside Shopping Center

narrative: On February 11, 2023, at approximately 2209 hours, officers were flagged down by the victim in the public parking lot at 1800 Washington Way, Greenfield, regarding a stolen vehicle. The victim reported that a silver 2021 SUV, valued at $55,717, had been taken from the lot. The victim stated that the vehicle was left running with keys in the ignition while they briefly entered a nearby store. Upon returning, the victim observed the vehicle missing and immediately notified police. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and secured surveillance footage from adjacent businesses, which showed an unknown adult male suspect entering the vehicle at 2207 hours and driving northbound on Washington Way. Officers broadcast a description of the vehicle and suspect over radio. At approximately 2240 hours, patrol units located the stolen vehicle parked two blocks away with the suspect inside. The suspect was detained without incident and positively identified by the victim. The vehicle was returned to the victim undamaged. No injuries were reported.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1800 Washington Way

narrative: On September 10, 2023, at approximately 12:24 a.m., officers were dispatched to a reported burglary at a residence located in the 4100 block of Second Street, within the Industrial Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the rear door of the residence had been forcibly opened, with visible damage to the door frame and lock mechanism. The victim stated that only the master bedroom showed signs of disturbance, including opened drawers and displaced items. The victim reported the theft of computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $500 in cash, and various inventory items, with an estimated total loss of $14,947. Officers conducted a canvass of the surrounding area and spoke with nearby residents, but no witnesses or additional information was obtained. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Crime scene photographs were taken, and latent fingerprint evidence was collected from the door and bedroom surfaces. The investigation remains open pending further leads.
address_block: the 4100 block of Second Street

narrative: On April 6, 2023, at approximately 2057 hours, officers responded to a reported vehicle burglary at the 4300 block of River Street in the Industrial Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed that the garage door of the residence had visible pry marks consistent with the use of a crowbar. The victim stated that upon entering the home, only the master bedroom showed signs of disturbance, with drawers and cabinets left open. The victim reported the theft of a laptop computer, a gaming console, and prescription medications, with an estimated total loss of $2,500. Officers canvassed the immediate area but did not locate any witnesses. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers collected surveillance footage from a neighboring property which captured a suspect approaching the residence. The footage was logged into evidence for further review. No arrest was made at the scene; the victim was provided with a case information card and advised on follow-up procedures.
address_block: the 4300 block of River Street

narrative: On February 3, 2023, at approximately 0532 hours, officers responded to Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Harbor and Elm in the Sunset Heights neighborhood after being flagged down by a witness reporting a weapons discharge. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle parked near the entrance with its engine running. Witnesses on scene stated they observed the suspect, described as a male adult, discharge a firearm from the vehicle before quickly exiting and discarding the weapon under a nearby bench. Officers secured the area and located a semi-automatic handgun beneath the bench. The suspect was apprehended without incident and placed under arrest. No injuries were reported. Witnesses provided consistent statements indicating the discharge occurred but that no individuals were targeted. The recovered firearm was collected as evidence. Officers canvassed the area for additional evidence and damage, none was found. The suspect was transported for booking.
address_block: Industrial Park Park near the intersection of Harbor and Elm

narrative: On February 23, 2024, at approximately 0414 hours, officers were flagged down by the store clerk at the QuickMart convenience store located in the Westside Shopping Center, Millbrook neighborhood, regarding a suspected check fraud incident. The clerk reported that an unknown individual attempted to cash a check in the amount of $143,205, which appeared suspicious due to irregularities in the check’s printing and the lack of proper identification provided by the individual. The suspect, described as a male, mid-30s, approximately 6’0”, medium build, wearing a dark jacket and baseball cap, left the premises before officers arrived. Officers collected the fraudulent check, store surveillance footage, and a copy of the transaction log as evidence. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The incident was determined to be unfounded after further review revealed the check was never processed or cashed. The evidence was submitted to the crime lab for analysis, and the investigation is ongoing.
address_block: the QuickMart convenience store in the Westside Shopping Center

narrative: On July 23, 2023, at approximately 8:08 AM, officers on routine patrol in the Greenfield neighborhood were flagged down by a concerned citizen in the public parking lot located at 2000 Second Way. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject, later identified as the suspect, seated inside a parked vehicle. Multiple witnesses at the scene reported observing the suspect handling what appeared to be drug paraphernalia, specifically a glass pipe commonly associated with narcotics use. Officers approached the vehicle and observed the glass pipe in plain view on the passenger seat. The suspect was detained without incident. A subsequent search of the vehicle, based on probable cause, revealed additional items consistent with drug use, including a small digital scale and burnt foil. The suspect was advised of his rights and admitted to possessing the paraphernalia for personal use. No injuries were reported. The suspect was arrested and transported for booking. All evidence was collected, photographed, and submitted to property for further analysis.
address_block: the public parking lot at 2000 Second Way

narrative: On July 4, 2024, at approximately 2:18 AM, officers responded to a report of drug paraphernalia at the 7-Eleven located in the Downtown Shopping Center, Old Town neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect standing near the entrance, displaying suspicious behavior. Store personnel reported witnessing the suspect handling a glass pipe commonly used for narcotics consumption inside the premises. Officers approached the suspect, conducted a field interview, and subsequently performed a search, locating the glass pipe and a small plastic bag containing residue consistent with illegal substances. The suspect denied ownership of the items but was placed under arrest for possession of drug paraphernalia. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Evidence was photographed and collected for further analysis. The investigation remains ongoing. Witnesses were provided with contact information should they have additional information regarding the incident.
address_block: the 7-Eleven in the Downtown Shopping Center

narrative: On March 26, 2024, at approximately 2028 hours, officers were dispatched to the Best Buy electronics store at 8800 Lake Boulevard in response to a reported public disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed several individuals gathered near the store entrance but noted no active altercation or signs of distress. Store management stated that a customer had raised his voice regarding a service issue, prompting staff to contact police out of concern for escalating behavior. The involved customer was interviewed and cooperated fully, explaining frustration over a delayed product pickup but denying any threats or aggressive conduct. Witnesses present corroborated that no physical confrontation or threats occurred. Officers conducted a walkthrough of the premises and found no evidence of property damage or injury. The situation was deemed unfounded, and no arrests were made. All parties were advised and dispersed without further incident.
address_block: the Best Buy electronics store located at 8800 Lake Boulevard

narrative: On June 13, 2024, at approximately 0652 hours, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot located at 1800 Hill Way in the Eastgate neighborhood in response to a reported credit card fraud. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect seated in a parked sedan, actively attempting multiple transactions using various credit cards on a portable card reader. Officers made contact with the suspect, who was unable to provide valid identification or account for the source of the cards in his possession. The victim, who had received alerts regarding unauthorized charges totaling $10,616, arrived on scene and confirmed no consent had been given for these transactions. Two witnesses were interviewed and each stated that they observed the suspect using multiple cards and acting suspiciously near parked vehicles. Officers collected the fraudulent cards, electronic devices, and transaction records as evidence. The suspect was placed under arrest without incident and transported for booking. No injuries or weapons were reported.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1800 Hill Way

narrative: On April 19, 2024, at approximately 1150 hours, officers were flagged down by a resident in the 6000 block of Washington Avenue, Riverside neighborhood, regarding a reported vehicle vandalism. Upon arrival, officers observed a gray four-door sedan parked along the curbside with multiple scratches along the driver’s side door and a shattered rear window. The reporting party, identified as the vehicle owner, stated the damage was discovered upon returning to the vehicle at approximately 1145 hours and had not noticed any suspicious individuals in the vicinity. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with nearby residents, none of whom reported witnessing the incident. No surveillance cameras were observed in the immediate area. Photographs of the damage were taken, and glass fragments were collected as evidence for processing by the crime lab. The estimated loss was reported at $6,830. No suspects were identified, and no arrests were made. The incident was determined to be unfounded based on lack of evidence or witness corroboration.
address_block: the 6000 block of Washington Avenue

narrative: On April 12, 2023, at approximately 0031 hours, officers were dispatched to the liquor store at 7500 Cedar Boulevard, Eastgate neighborhood, regarding a suspected drug distribution. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject standing near the southeast corner of the building, engaging in what appeared to be a hand-to-hand transaction with another individual. Both subjects were detained without incident. The area was secured, and a field interview was conducted. The first subject admitted to providing a small quantity of suspected narcotics in exchange for cash. Officers recovered a clear plastic bag containing a white powdery substance from the suspect’s person, as well as a small amount of cash. Both subjects declined medical assistance and reported no injuries. No weapons were found. The suspect did not attempt to force entry into any buildings and no property damage or theft was reported. Officers interviewed the suspect, who claimed he was cutting through the property to reach a nearby bus stop. No injuries or weapons were involved. Officers made contact with the individual, who verbally identified themselves and complied with commands. A cursory search revealed a small, clear plastic bag containing a substance consistent in appearance with marijuana. The individual denied ownership of the substance and stated they had found it on the ground moments prior to officer arrival. No other witnesses were present at the scene, and a canvass of the immediate area yielded no additional information. The primary individual responsible for the speaker, described as an adult male, was uncooperative and refused to lower the volume when directed. After repeated warnings, the individual was cited for violation of the noise ordinance and placed under arrest for failure to comply.
