The suspect then exited the store and fled the area in a dark-colored vehicle, direction unknown. The victim sustained minor injuries during the incident, reportedly from being pushed by the suspect. narrative: On November 13, 2023, at approximately 1845 hours, officers responded to a report of a suspected impaired driver at a retail store located in the 2400 block of Monroe Drive, Cedar Grove neighborhood. Officers collected physical evidence, including the PBT device printout and video recordings from body-worn cameras. The evidence was logged and will be forwarded to the crime lab for analysis. Upon arrival, officers spoke with the reporting party, who stated that an unknown individual was observed loitering near the bank's exterior ATM, attempting to access the lobby after business hours. The suspect was described as a male, mid-30s, wearing dark clothing and a backpack. Officers conducted a canvass of the immediate area but were unable to locate the suspect or any additional witnesses. No signs of forced entry or property damage were observed, and no injuries were reported. Surveillance footage was reviewed and documented for follow-up. The area was cleared, and the case was closed due to lack of evidence and inability to identify or apprehend the suspect.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank in the Sunset Heights Shopping Center

narrative: On August 28, 2023, at approximately 1:46 PM, officers were dispatched to the Best Buy electronics store located within the Greenfield Shopping Center in the Midtown neighborhood regarding a reported auto theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that their vehicle, a 2022 luxury SUV with an estimated value of $60,372, had been stolen from the parking lot. The victim reported that a spare key was hidden inside a magnetic box under the rear bumper and believed the suspect located and utilized the key to access and drive away the vehicle. Officers canvassed the area and interviewed multiple witnesses, all of whom consistently reported seeing a male suspect in dark clothing loitering near the vehicle before entering and departing in it. Surveillance footage was obtained from Best Buy, confirming the sequence of events. Officers quickly broadcasted the suspect and vehicle description, resulting in the suspect being located and arrested without incident nearby. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved.
address_block: the Best Buy electronics store in the Greenfield Shopping Center

narrative: On March 13, 2023, at approximately 1:18 AM, officers were dispatched to an apartment complex located in the 5300 block of Hill Road, Parkview neighborhood, in response to a reported vehicle burglary. Upon arrival, officers met with the reporting party, who stated that unknown suspect(s) had gained entry to a business vehicle via a dog door that appeared to have been forcibly enlarged. Officers observed signs of forced entry and noted that multiple compartments within the vehicle had been searched, with various closet and storage doors left open. The victim reported the theft of computer equipment, a cash register containing approximately $2,500 in U.S. currency, and assorted inventory items, with an estimated total loss of $13,278. Officers canvassed the surrounding area, speaking with nearby residents and checking surveillance cameras, but no additional witnesses or viable leads were identified. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The case was determined to be unfounded due to insufficient evidence linking a suspect to the scene.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 5300 block of Hill Road

narrative: On November 10, 2023, at approximately 2009 hours, officers were dispatched to the 5400 block of Oak Street, Old Town neighborhood, regarding a reported domestic violence incident involving an assault with a blunt object. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult female, seated on the front walkway of the residence, holding her head and exhibiting visible facial swelling and bleeding from the nose. The victim stated she had been struck during a verbal altercation with her partner inside the home. Officers canvassed the area and contacted a male subject inside the residence, who denied involvement and showed no signs of injury. No weapons were located at the scene. Paramedics arrived and transported the victim to the hospital for treatment of a suspected broken nose and facial contusions. Witness statements from two neighbors indicated loud arguing prior to the incident but did not directly observe the assault. No arrest was made at this time, and the investigation was referred to detectives for further follow-up.
address_block: the 5400 block of Oak Street

narrative: On December 13, 2023, at approximately 10:29 PM, patrol officers responded to a report of wire fraud at the public parking lot located at 2700 Hill Way in the North Hills neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that an individual had solicited a wire transfer under false pretenses, resulting in a financial loss of $11,464. The suspect was present at the scene and identified by the victim. Officers detained the suspect without incident. A preliminary investigation revealed electronic correspondence and transaction records on the victim's mobile device, which were documented and collected as evidence. Witnesses in the vicinity confirmed the interaction between the victim and suspect prior to the wire transfer. The suspect was arrested and transported to the station for further questioning. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. All evidence related to the fraudulent transaction was secured and submitted to the crime lab for analysis.
address_block: the public parking lot at 2700 Hill Way

narrative: On April 11, 2024, at approximately 2:21 AM, officers on patrol in the Industrial Park neighborhood were flagged down by a security guard regarding fresh graffiti vandalism at a commercial property on the 3700 block of Main Street. Upon arrival, officers observed multiple large spray-painted tags in various colors across the north-facing exterior wall and loading dock doors. The damage appeared recent, with paint still wet in some areas. No suspects were present on scene and the security guard reported hearing voices and seeing shadows near the wall minutes prior to flagging down officers but could not provide detailed descriptions. Officers photographed the graffiti, collected paint chips, and obtained surveillance footage from nearby cameras. Crime lab processing was requested for potential identification. Estimated damage to the property was assessed at $10,974. No injuries or weapons were reported. The case was closed pending further investigative leads.
address_block: the 3700 block of Main Street

narrative: On October 27, 2024, at approximately 1926 hours, officers were flagged down in the 3000 block of Main Drive by a store employee regarding a disturbance at a retail store. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the reporting party, who stated that loud music and shouting had been coming from inside the store for approximately 30 minutes, disturbing customers and adjacent businesses. Officers entered the store and observed several individuals congregated near the electronics section, where a portable speaker was playing music at a high volume. No physical altercations or visible injuries were observed. Officers requested that the individuals lower the volume and cease disruptive behavior. All parties complied without incident. Officers documented the scene by taking photographs and collecting a copy of the store’s surveillance footage as evidence. No arrests were made, and no weapons or injuries were reported. The case remains open pending further investigation into repeated complaints.
address_block: a retail store in the 3000 block of Main Drive

narrative: On November 27, 2024, at approximately 1934 hours, officers were flagged down by the victim at the intersection of Elm Street and Meadow Avenue in the Bayshore neighborhood regarding a credit card fraud incident. The victim reported unauthorized transactions totaling approximately $146,582 on their credit card account. The victim stated they had not lost possession of their card and first noticed the fraudulent charges earlier that day when reviewing their account online. Officers interviewed the victim at the scene and obtained a statement detailing the timeline of discovery and recent card usage. No suspects were observed in the immediate vicinity. Officers canvassed nearby businesses and secured surveillance footage from a convenience store located at the intersection. The footage is being reviewed for any individuals making suspicious purchases or attempting to use the victim's credit card. No injuries were reported, no weapon was involved, and no arrests have been made. The case has been closed pending further leads.
address_block: the intersection of Elm Street and Meadow Avenue

narrative: On November 2, 2023, at approximately 9:48 AM, patrol officers responded to a reported battery in the 7500 block of Elm Avenue, Millbrook neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a group of bystanders actively separating the victim, an adult male, from the suspect, an adult female. The victim was visibly injured with swelling and bleeding to the nose and facial area, and reported being struck multiple times in the face by the suspect during a verbal altercation. Officers rendered first aid until EMS arrived and subsequently transported the victim to the hospital for treatment of a possible broken nose and facial contusions. The suspect remained on scene and provided a statement, claiming self-defense. Several witnesses were identified and their contact information was collected. Officers canvassed the area for surveillance cameras and secured footage from a nearby residence that captured the incident. The investigation is ongoing and no arrests have been made at this time.
address_block: the 7500 block of Elm Avenue

narrative: On August 12, 2024, at approximately 2129 hours, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 1600 block of Meadow Drive in the Harbor District regarding a reported property destruction incident. Upon arrival, officers contacted store management, who reported discovering several large plate glass windows at the store’s front entrance shattered. Management stated the damage was observed upon closing procedures and estimated the loss at $9,429. Officers observed broken glass scattered on the sidewalk but found no signs of forced entry or items missing from the premises. A canvass of the immediate area was conducted; no additional witnesses or surveillance footage capturing the event were located. No suspect description was available, and no injuries were reported. Due to lack of evidence or leads, the incident was determined to be unfounded at this time. Officers advised management to contact police if further information or video evidence became available.
address_block: a retail store in the 1600 block of Meadow Drive

narrative: On July 14, 2024, at approximately 11:46 PM, officers were dispatched to Cedar Grove Park near the intersection of Lake and Pine in the Sunset Heights neighborhood regarding a reported weapons offense involving illegal possession. Upon arrival, officers conducted a systematic check of the park but did not observe any individuals matching the description provided by the reporting party, nor was any suspect located in the immediate area. Officers spoke with a witness who reported seeing an unknown male, approximately 20-30 years old, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans, handling what appeared to be a firearm near a park bench before leaving on foot westbound toward Pine Street. No injuries were reported and no weapons were located at the scene. Officers canvassed for additional witnesses and secured surveillance footage from nearby cameras for further review. The case remains open pending identification of the suspect and additional investigative leads.
address_block: Cedar Grove Park near the intersection of Lake and Pine

narrative: On August 4, 2024, at approximately 1746 hours, officers responded to a report of simple assault in the 2200 block of Pine Street, Riverside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult, seated on the sidewalk, holding their head and appearing visibly distressed. Officers conducted a preliminary assessment and noted no visible injuries; however, the victim complained of pain to the jaw and stated they had been struck during an altercation. The victim reported that the suspect, described as an unknown male, brandished a firearm during the incident but did not discharge the weapon. The suspect fled the scene prior to officers' arrival. No witnesses were present at the time, and no property loss was reported. Officers canvassed the area for surveillance footage and collected statements from the victim. The case was referred to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: the 2200 block of Pine Street

narrative: On June 28, 2024, at approximately 1830 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported criminal trespass at a single-family residence located in the Sunset Heights area of the Downtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the resident, who stated that an unknown individual had entered the fenced backyard without permission and was observed near the rear door. The resident reported that upon being confronted, the suspect quickly exited through the side gate and fled in an unknown direction. Officers conducted a thorough check of the property and surrounding area but were unable to locate the suspect. No forced entry was observed, and no property damage or loss was reported. The resident provided a general description of the suspect, but no surveillance footage was available. Officers documented the scene and advised the resident on security measures. The case was forwarded to detectives for further investigation. No injuries were reported, and no arrests were made at the time.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Downtown neighborhood

narrative: On October 1, 2024, at approximately 12:45 PM, officers were flagged down by a resident at a single-family home in the Harbor District, Greenfield neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a sedan parked in the driveway with its front door lock showing signs consistent with being picked. The homeowner reported leaving the residence at 9:00 AM and returning shortly before contacting police. Officers entered the home and noted the interior was ransacked, with furniture overturned and drawers emptied in the living room and master bedroom. The victim reported missing electronics, several pieces of jewelry, and an undetermined amount of cash, with the estimated loss totaling $4,394. A canvass of the area led to contact with a neighbor who witnessed an unknown male suspect leaving the scene carrying a duffel bag. Officers located a subject matching the description nearby, detained him, and recovered stolen property in his possession. The suspect was arrested without incident. Photographs were taken, latent prints collected, and all evidence secured for processing. No injuries were reported.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Harbor District neighborhood

narrative: On February 6, 2024, at approximately 2132 hours, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the South Valley neighborhood of the Harbor District in response to a reported DUI collision with injury. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle stopped on the front lawn with visible front-end damage. The driver, an adult male, was found seated behind the wheel and exhibited signs of intoxication, including slurred speech, bloodshot eyes, and an unsteady gait. The victim, a resident of the home, reported minor injuries sustained when the suspect’s vehicle struck a parked car, causing debris to strike her leg. Officers administered standardized field sobriety tests, which the driver failed. A preliminary breath test indicated a blood alcohol concentration of 0.14%. The suspect was placed under arrest for DUI with injury and transported for booking. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; however, no additional individuals were located. Photos of the scene and vehicles were taken and entered into evidence.
address_block: a single-family residence in the South Valley neighborhood

narrative: On August 8, 2023, at approximately 3:39 AM, patrol officers responded to a report of vehicle vandalism at a retail store located in the 6500 block of Park Drive, Midtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a white SUV parked in the lot with extensive damage to the windshield, side mirrors, and body panels. The victim stated the vehicle was parked overnight and discovered the damage upon arrival for work. Officers interviewed two witnesses, both store employees, who reported hearing loud noises near the parking area around 3:30 AM. One witness observed an unidentified individual wearing dark clothing fleeing the scene on foot. No suspect was located during a canvas of the area. Officers documented the damage, photographed the scene, and collected surveillance footage from the store’s cameras for review. No injuries were reported. The estimated value of the damage was $8,450. The case remains open pending further investigation.
address_block: a retail store in the 6500 block of Park Drive

narrative: On March 11, 2023, at approximately 1620 hours, officers were dispatched to a reported commercial burglary in the 7400 block of Lincoln Avenue, Old Town neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the front door lock of the business showed clear signs of tampering consistent with lock picking. The interior appeared ransacked, with multiple pieces of furniture overturned in the main office area. The victim, a store manager on scene, stated that a laptop computer, gaming console, and a quantity of prescription medications had been stolen, with an estimated total loss of $9,369. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses, but none were present at the time of the incident. Surveillance footage from the premises was collected for evidence and is currently under review for suspect identification. The scene was processed for fingerprints and other forensic evidence. The case is closed due to lack of suspect information and investigative leads at this time.
address_block: the 7400 block of Lincoln Avenue

narrative: On March 5, 2023, at approximately 1:10 AM, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Harbor Street and First Avenue in the South Valley neighborhood regarding a reported carjacking. Upon arrival, officers located the victim, a 24-year-old male, standing near the curb with visible lacerations to his right forearm and minor contusions to his face. The victim stated he was entering his vehicle, a silver 2019 sedan, when an unknown male suspect approached on foot from the north side of Harbor Street. The suspect, described as approximately 5'10", medium build, wearing dark clothing and a hooded sweatshirt, brandished a blunt object resembling a metal pipe and struck the victim on the arm. The suspect ordered the victim out of the vehicle and threatened further harm. Fearing for his safety, the victim complied and exited the vehicle. The suspect entered the driver’s seat and fled eastbound on Harbor Street. Officers secured the scene and requested EMS, who treated the victim’s injuries on site. A canvass for witnesses was conducted; one nearby resident reported hearing a commotion but did not see the incident. Officers processed the scene for evidence, including lifting possible latent prints from the vehicle door handle and recovering a dropped wallet belonging to the victim. The stolen vehicle was entered into the statewide database. The investigation remains open and has been assigned to detectives for follow-up.
address_block: the intersection of Harbor Street and First Avenue

narrative: On February 9, 2023, at approximately 1855 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Adams Street and Pine Avenue in the University District in response to a reported public disturbance. Upon arrival, officers canvassed the area and observed a small group of individuals gathered on the sidewalk, engaged in a verbal dispute. No physical altercations or threats were witnessed, and all parties denied knowledge of any ongoing disturbance. Officers interviewed several bystanders, none of whom reported seeing any criminal activity or aggressive behavior. Surveillance footage from a nearby business was secured for review; preliminary examination showed no evidence of a disturbance escalating beyond raised voices. No weapons were observed or reported, and there were no injuries or property damage. Officers determined the complaint to be unfounded and cleared the scene without further incident.
address_block: the intersection of Adams Street and Pine Avenue

narrative: On October 27, 2023, at approximately 4:58 AM, officers responded to a report of a domestic violence incident in the 3200 block of Adams Avenue, South Valley. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim seated on the curb with a visible laceration to the forehead. The victim stated that during a verbal altercation with a known suspect inside a parked vehicle, the suspect accelerated the vehicle abruptly, causing the victim to strike their head against the interior. The suspect fled the scene in the vehicle prior to officer arrival. Medical personnel were summoned and provided treatment to the victim on scene. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspect or the vehicle. Witnesses in the vicinity were interviewed and corroborated the victim’s account of the incident, stating they observed the suspect’s rapid departure. No significant property loss was reported. Based on investigation and witness statements, the incident was determined to be unfounded for criminal charges at this time.
address_block: the 3200 block of Adams Avenue

narrative: On February 9, 2024, at approximately 3:07 AM, officers were dispatched to the 5400 block of Hill Avenue in the Midtown neighborhood in response to a reported disturbance involving excessive noise. Upon arrival, officers observed loud music and shouting coming from an apartment unit on the second floor. Officers made contact with the occupants, including the suspect, who was uncooperative and refused to lower the volume despite multiple requests. Several residents in neighboring units, identified as witnesses, reported ongoing disturbances and provided statements regarding the impact of the noise. The suspect was placed under arrest for disorderly conduct. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers collected audio recordings of the noise using department-issued equipment and documented statements from witnesses. All evidence was secured for processing by the crime lab. The scene was cleared without further incident. Estimated loss is $0.
address_block: the 5400 block of Hill Avenue

narrative: On July 7, 2024, at approximately 6:41 AM, officers were dispatched to Oak Park Park near the intersection of River and First in response to a report of illegal weapon possession. Upon arrival, officers conducted a thorough canvass of the park and surrounding area and made contact with several individuals present. No weapons were observed in plain sight and all subjects denied possessing or having knowledge of any firearms or other prohibited weapons. Officers interviewed a reporting party who stated they believed someone in the park was in possession of a weapon but could not provide a specific description of the individual or the alleged weapon. No evidence of illegal possession was located, and no injuries were reported. Officers documented the incident and advised all parties of the complaint. The case was referred to detectives for follow-up investigation. The incident was determined to be unfounded and no arrests were made.
address_block: Oak Park Park near the intersection of River and First

narrative: On August 8, 2024, at approximately 6:05 AM, officers responded to the public parking lot at 8700 Monroe Way in the Millbrook neighborhood after being flagged down by the victim regarding a grand theft. The victim reported that their vehicle, parked overnight, had been unlawfully entered and personal property valued at approximately $2,096 was removed. Officers observed no signs of forced entry on the vehicle. The victim provided a description of the suspect, who was observed leaving the scene on foot. Officers conducted a canvass of the area and spoke to nearby individuals; however, no additional witnesses were located. The suspect was located a short distance away and detained. Stolen property was recovered in the suspect’s possession. The suspect was cited and arrested at the scene. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers documented the recovered property and completed evidence collection procedures.
address_block: the public parking lot at 8700 Monroe Way

narrative: On June 20, 2024, at approximately 1559 hours, officers were dispatched to a retail store located in the 4200 block of First Drive, Bayshore, regarding a report of possible drug distribution. Upon arrival, officers made contact with store management, who stated that an individual had been observed exchanging small packets with multiple persons in the store parking lot. Officers observed the described suspect, an adult male, standing near the entrance and matching the provided description. Upon approach, the suspect attempted to conceal several small baggies containing a white powdery substance consistent with narcotics. The suspect was detained without incident. A field test of the substance yielded a presumptive positive result for cocaine. The suspect was placed under arrest for distribution of a controlled substance. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Surveillance footage and physical evidence were collected. The investigation is ongoing, and any witnesses are encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: a retail store in the 4200 block of First Drive

narrative: On December 13, 2024, at approximately 4:57 AM, officers responded to a report of a possible DUI in the public parking lot at 2600 Second Way, Oak Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle parked askew with the engine running. Contact was made with the driver, who exhibited slurred speech and had difficulty recalling recent events or their location. The driver appeared disoriented and showed signs of impairment. Officers administered standardized field sobriety tests, including the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand, all of which the subject failed. A portable breath test was conducted, showing a BAC of 0.17%. The subject was placed under arrest for DUI. No injuries or weapons were reported. Officers conducted a canvass of the area; no witnesses were identified. The subject was cited and released per protocol. No property loss was reported.
address_block: the public parking lot at 2600 Second Way

narrative: On September 28, 2023, at approximately 1:42 AM, officers responded to a reported strong-arm robbery at a retail store located in the 2600 block of River Drive, Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers observed the victim, an adult store clerk, visibly shaken and seated near the cash register with minor injuries to the left forearm. The victim reported that a male suspect entered the store, approached from behind, and brandished a black handgun, demanding the victim’s wallet and mobile phone. The victim complied, and the suspect fled on foot with approximately $79 in cash and the phone. Officers conducted a canvass of the surrounding area but did not locate additional witnesses. Surveillance footage was reviewed, capturing the suspect’s description: male, mid-20s, wearing a dark hooded sweatshirt and jeans. Officers located the suspect nearby, matching the description, and recovered the stolen property and firearm upon arrest. The victim was treated by EMS at the scene. The suspect was transported for booking.
address_block: a retail store in the 2600 block of River Drive

narrative: On October 26, 2024, at approximately 2048 hours, officers responded to the Best Buy electronics store at 5200 Lake Boulevard, South Valley, after being flagged down by store employees regarding an armed robbery. Upon arrival, officers located the victim, an adult male employee, near the customer service counter. The victim stated that a male suspect entered the store, approached the counter, and produced what appeared to be a blunt object, possibly a metal pipe, not a firearm as initially reported. The suspect demanded cash from the register and struck the victim on the left arm when he hesitated, causing minor injury. The suspect then removed approximately $9,793 from the register and fled the location on foot in an unknown direction. Officers canvassed the area but did not locate the suspect. Surveillance footage was recovered, and statements were obtained from two witnesses, both store employees, who corroborated the victim’s account. The case was assigned to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: the Best Buy electronics store located at 5200 Lake Boulevard

narrative: On April 11, 2023, at approximately 7:47 AM, patrol officers responded to a reported unlawful entry at an apartment complex located in the 3000 block of Second Road, within the Harbor District. Upon arrival, officers met with the apartment manager, who stated that a resident observed an unknown individual entering a restricted maintenance area without authorization. Officers conducted a search of the premises but did not locate any suspects. No property damage or theft was reported, and no injuries occurred. Surveillance footage from the complex was obtained and is currently under review to identify the suspect. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with two residents who confirmed seeing a male subject, approximately 5’10” with dark clothing, enter the area at around 7:40 AM. No arrest was made at the time of the report. The investigation remains open pending further review of evidence.
address_block: an apartment complex in the 3000 block of Second Road

narrative: On August 15, 2023, at approximately 0800 hours, officers responded to a report of a residential burglary at a single-family residence located in the 1600 block of Main Avenue, Midtown. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated they had left the residence unoccupied since 0700 hours. Officers observed that entry appeared to have been gained through a dog door at the rear of the home, which had been forcibly enlarged, causing visible damage to the frame. Inside, officers noted several rooms had been ransacked, with closet doors open and contents displaced. The victim reported electronics, assorted jewelry, and an undetermined amount of cash missing, with a total estimated loss of $8,089. There were no signs of forced entry at other access points. No injuries were reported. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and surveillance footage. One neighbor reported seeing an unfamiliar individual loitering near the residence around 0730 hours. The suspect was later located nearby, cited, and taken into custody without incident. The case was forwarded to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: the 1600 block of Main Avenue

narrative: On March 25, 2024, at approximately 11:01 AM, patrol units responded to a report of suspected drug distribution at the Wells Fargo bank located at 1600 Elm Boulevard in the North Hills neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect near the bank entrance engaged in a hand-to-hand transaction with an unidentified individual. Officers detained the suspect, who was found to be in possession of multiple small plastic bags containing a substance believed to be cocaine. Bank employees and two witnesses stated they observed the suspect approach several individuals and exchange items for cash. Officers conducted witness interviews, and all accounts were consistent regarding the suspect’s actions. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. The suspect was placed under arrest for drug distribution. Evidence, including the suspected narcotics and surveillance footage, was collected and submitted for further investigation.
address_block: the Wells Fargo bank located at 1600 Elm Boulevard

narrative: On June 9, 2023, at approximately 12:03 AM, officers were dispatched to the 4600 block of Lincoln Avenue, Downtown neighborhood, in response to a reported vehicle vandalism. Upon arrival, officers observed a black sedan parked curbside with extensive damage, including shattered windows and deep scratches along the driver’s side panels. The vehicle owner, identified as the victim, stated they had parked the car at approximately 11:15 PM and discovered the damage upon returning. No suspects were observed in the vicinity, and there were no surveillance cameras directly covering the area. Officers conducted a canvass of the block, interviewing nearby residents and businesses, but no witnesses or additional information was obtained. Photographs of the damage were taken for evidence. The estimated loss was reported at $6,251. No arrests were made, no injuries occurred, and the scene was cleared at 12:38 AM.
address_block: the 4600 block of Lincoln Avenue

narrative: On July 19, 2023, at approximately 2140 hours, officers were dispatched to the 900 block of Third Street in the Riverside neighborhood in response to a reported auto theft. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the victim, who stated that their vehicle, a 2022 luxury SUV valued at approximately $41,960, had been parked and secured in front of their residence at 1930 hours. The victim confirmed possession of both sets of keys and reported no signs of forced entry or broken glass at the scene. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses; a neighbor reported observing an unfamiliar vehicle idling nearby around 2100 hours but did not observe the theft. Officers obtained and secured surveillance footage from a nearby residence, which showed an unknown individual approaching the vehicle and entering it within seconds, consistent with a possible relay attack or electronic bypass. No injuries were reported. The investigation determined there was insufficient evidence of an actual theft, and the report was classified as unfounded.
address_block: the 900 block of Third Street

narrative: On October 28, 2023, at approximately 1:53 AM, officers were dispatched to the Shell gas station located within the Oak Park Shopping Center in the Midtown neighborhood in response to reports of a public disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed a male subject, later identified as the suspect, yelling loudly and engaging in aggressive behavior toward patrons near the fuel pumps. Several witnesses stated the suspect had been shouting obscenities and threatening customers, causing alarm. Officers made contact with the suspect, who appeared agitated and refused verbal commands to calm down. After repeated warnings, the suspect continued to disrupt the peace and was taken into custody without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were observed or recovered. Officers collected video surveillance footage from the gas station and obtained written statements from witnesses. Evidence was secured and submitted to the crime lab for analysis. The suspect was transported to the county jail for booking on charges of public disturbance.
address_block: the Shell gas station in the Oak Park Shopping Center

narrative: On October 25, 2024, at approximately 8:09 AM, patrol units responded to a reported theft from vehicle at the intersection of Maple Street and Adams Avenue in the Industrial Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers contacted the victim, who stated that an unknown male suspect was observed removing several electronic tools and equipment valued at approximately $9,770 from the unlocked rear compartment of the victim’s parked work van. The victim provided a description of the suspect as a male, medium build, wearing a dark hoodie and jeans. Officers canvassed the area and located the suspect matching the description walking eastbound on Adams Avenue, carrying a duffel bag containing items later identified as belonging to the victim. The suspect was detained without incident and positively identified by the victim. The suspect was cited for theft and transported for booking. No injuries were reported. Evidence, including recovered property and surveillance footage from a nearby business, was collected. The case has been assigned to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: the intersection of Maple Street and Adams Avenue

narrative: On March 8, 2023, at approximately 1613 hours, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Maple Street and Oak Avenue in the South Valley neighborhood in response to a reported noise disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed a group of approximately six individuals congregated near the northwest corner, playing amplified music at a high volume from a portable speaker. Several nearby residents were present and appeared visibly disturbed by the noise. Officers made contact with the individuals responsible, advised them of the complaint, and requested that the music be turned down. The individuals complied without incident. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with two residents who reported ongoing loud music issues at this location but did not wish to provide formal statements at this time. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were observed or involved. No arrests were made. The incident remains open and has been referred to detectives for follow-up investigation regarding repeated disturbances.
address_block: the intersection of Maple Street and Oak Avenue

narrative: On December 17, 2024, at approximately 1541 hours, officers on patrol in the South Valley neighborhood were flagged down by a store employee at the QuickMart convenience store, located in the Old Town Shopping Center. The employee reported observing an individual inside the store in possession of suspected illegal narcotics. Upon arrival, officers made contact with the individual, later identified as the suspect, who was found to have a small quantity of a substance believed to be methamphetamine in their possession. The suspect was cooperative and provided identification upon request. Officers conducted a search of the suspect and the immediate area; no weapons were found. The substance was collected and submitted for laboratory analysis. No injuries were reported and no arrest was made at the scene. Officers canvassed the surrounding area and interviewed available store patrons and staff; no additional witnesses or surveillance footage were located. The case was closed pending further investigation.
address_block: the QuickMart convenience store in the Old Town Shopping Center

narrative: On September 7, 2024, at approximately 1648 hours, officers were dispatched to a single-family residence in the Lakefront neighborhood of Bayshore regarding a reported vehicle burglary. Upon arrival, officers observed a shattered driver-side window on a sedan parked in the residence’s driveway, with glass debris scattered both inside the vehicle and near the entryway of the attached business office. The victim stated that upon entering the office area, which is accessible from the garage, they discovered multiple file cabinet drawers open and personal belongings displaced, consistent with a targeted search. The victim reported the theft of a laptop computer, gaming console, and prescription medications, collectively valued at approximately $3784. No injuries were reported and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area and spoke with neighbors, but no witnesses to the incident were identified. Upon arrival, officers observed an adult male, later identified as the suspect, seated on a park bench with various items, including a glass pipe and small plastic bags commonly associated with narcotics use, visible on the ground nearby. Officers detained the suspect and conducted a pat-down for officer safety. No weapons were located. Two witnesses present provided consistent statements indicating they observed the suspect handling the pipe and preparing to use it. The suspect admitted possession of the items but denied recent drug use. Officers collected the paraphernalia as evidence, photographed the scene, and cited the suspect for possession of drug paraphernalia. No injuries were reported, and no estimated loss was involved. The suspect was released on scene following issuance of the citation.

narrative: On July 29, 2024, at approximately 7:08 AM, officers were dispatched to the Starbucks coffee shop located at 2600 Lake Boulevard in response to a reported petty theft. The manager reported that no physical altercation had occurred, and no weapons were involved. Surveillance footage was reviewed on scene, but no suspicious activity was observed during the relevant time frame. Several employees present during the shift were interviewed, all of whom denied knowledge of the missing funds. No customers were reported to have interacted with the register. No injuries were reported. Based on available evidence, officers determined the incident to be unfounded at this time. The case was referred to detectives for further investigation, and no arrests were made.

narrative: On June 17, 2023, at approximately 11:24 PM, patrol officers responded to a call regarding an unlawful entry at a retail store located in the 8900 block of Harbor Drive, Midtown neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed the suspect inside the store after business hours, despite clearly posted signage indicating the premises were closed. Store management confirmed the suspect did not have permission to enter and had bypassed a locked entry door without force. Officers detained the suspect without incident; no weapons were found, and no injuries were reported. The suspect was advised of their rights and provided a verbal statement, admitting to entering the property to "look around." Surveillance footage capturing the entry was collected and logged as evidence for further processing by the crime lab. No property loss or damage was identified. The suspect was transported to the precinct for booking on trespassing charges.
address_block: a retail store in the 8900 block of Harbor Drive

narrative: On February 29, 2024, at approximately 1:54 PM, officers were dispatched to the intersection of Lake Street and Valley Avenue in the Highland neighborhood regarding a reported weapons offense involving brandishing. Upon arrival, officers observed a male suspect standing on the northwest corner, holding a metal pipe in a threatening manner. The victim, an adult female, stated that the suspect approached her while she was walking, raised the pipe, and made verbal threats, causing her to fear for her safety. Officers secured the scene and located the metal pipe near the sidewalk; it was photographed and collected as evidence for processing by the crime lab. Witnesses at a nearby bus stop corroborated the victim’s account, describing the suspect’s aggressive behavior. The suspect fled prior to police arrival and was not located during an area search. No injuries were reported, and the investigation remains open pending further identification of the suspect.
address_block: the intersection of Lake Street and Valley Avenue

narrative: On March 7, 2024, at approximately 12:47 PM, officers were dispatched to the 2000 block of Adams Street in the Highland neighborhood in response to a reported public disturbance. Upon arrival, officers observed a male adult, later identified as the suspect, shouting loudly and causing a disruption on the sidewalk. Several bystanders were present and appeared alarmed by the suspect’s behavior. Officers approached and made contact with the suspect, who was uncooperative but did not possess any weapons. Witnesses stated the suspect had been yelling profanities and obstructing pedestrian traffic for several minutes. Officers attempted to de-escalate the situation and issued verbal warnings, but the suspect refused to comply. The suspect was subsequently cited for public disturbance and placed under arrest without incident. No injuries were reported and no property damage occurred. The case was referred to detectives for further investigation.
address_block: the 2000 block of Adams Street

narrative: On May 23, 2024, at approximately 5:32 AM, officers were flagged down by the victim at the intersection of Lake Street and Washington Avenue in the Oak Park neighborhood regarding a stolen vehicle. The victim reported that their vehicle, a 2022 dark gray sedan valued at approximately $37,045, had been parked and locked at the location overnight. The victim stated that both original key fobs were in their possession and had not been used since parking the vehicle. Officers observed no signs of forced entry or broken glass in the immediate area. The circumstances suggested a possible relay attack or electronic bypass method was used to access and start the vehicle. Officers canvassed the area for surveillance cameras and potential witnesses; no immediate leads were identified. The victim provided a written statement and vehicle details for entry into the national stolen vehicle database. No injuries were reported, and no suspects were identified at the scene. The investigation remains ongoing; individuals with information are encouraged to contact the department.
address_block: the intersection of Lake Street and Washington Avenue

Upon arrival, officers made contact with store employees who reported observing a male subject, later identified as the suspect, acting erratically near the rear of the store. Officers approached the suspect and noted the odor of marijuana emanating from his person. A consent search revealed a small clear plastic bag containing a green leafy substance consistent with marijuana, as well as a second bag containing a white powdery substance suspected to be cocaine. The suspect was detained without incident and placed under arrest for possession of a controlled substance. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Evidence was collected and logged. The suspect was transported to the precinct for processing. The case was assigned to detectives for further investigation.

Officers arrived at the location and conducted a thorough area check, locating the individual matching the provided description standing near a parked vehicle. The subject was detained for investigation, and officers conducted a consensual search; no firearm or illegal items were found. Officers interviewed nearby residents and canvassed the area for additional witnesses, but no one reported seeing a weapon or suspicious activity. The subject denied possessing a firearm and cooperated with officers. After a comprehensive investigation, no evidence of illegal weapon possession was discovered, and the incident was determined to be unfounded. No arrests were made and no injuries were reported. The investigation remains ongoing, and individuals with further information are encouraged to contact the department.

Officers approached the suspect and, during a consensual encounter, detected the odor of marijuana emanating from his person. A probable cause search was conducted, resulting in the discovery of a clear plastic bag containing a green leafy substance believed to be marijuana, as well as a small quantity of white powder later field-tested positive for cocaine. The suspect was detained without incident and read his Miranda rights; he admitted to possessing the substances for personal use. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were found. Officers canvassed the area, but no additional witnesses were located. The suspect was transported to the station for booking. Evidence was logged and submitted to property for further analysis.

Store employees reported that the suspect had entered the premises and began arguing with staff over a perceived issue with a returned item. Multiple witnesses stated the suspect ignored requests to calm down and continued disruptive behavior. Officers interviewed staff and witnesses, documenting their statements. No injuries were reported and no weapons were observed or involved. Surveillance footage was obtained and evidence was collected for further review by the crime lab. The suspect left the location prior to officer arrival and a follow-up investigation is ongoing. No arrests were made at the time of this report.
address_block: the auto parts store in the Bayshore Shopping Center

narrative: On October 22, 2023, at approximately 8:28 AM, officers were dispatched to the 8200 block of Adams Street in the Highland neighborhood regarding a suspected DUI collision with injury. Upon arrival, officers observed a sedan stopped partially on the curb with visible front-end damage. The driver, an adult male, was seated in the vehicle and exhibited slurred speech and bloodshot eyes. A strong odor of alcoholic beverage was detected emanating from the driver and the interior of the vehicle. The driver struggled to produce a valid driver’s license when requested. Officers noted minor injuries to the driver’s forearm, which were consistent with impact from the collision; medical personnel were summoned to the scene. Field sobriety tests were conducted, during which the driver failed the horizontal gaze nystagmus, walk-and-turn, and one-leg stand assessments. A preliminary breath test was administered, yielding a blood alcohol concentration of 0.20%. Officers canvassed the immediate area for witnesses; no additional persons reported observing the incident. The investigation was closed and no arrest was made at the time.
address_block: the 8200 block of Adams Street

narrative: On February 19, 2024, at approximately 2:12 AM, patrol units responded to a reported vandalism incident at a single-family residence located in the Parkview section of the Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers observed fresh graffiti consisting of black spray-painted symbols and letters on the front exterior wall facing the street. The homeowner, identified as the victim, reported hearing noises outside shortly after 2:00 AM and discovering the vandalism upon investigation. Officers canvassed the immediate area and interviewed two neighbors, both of whom reported seeing an unknown individual dressed in dark clothing leaving the scene on foot heading westbound at approximately the same time. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers documented the scene with photographs and collected video footage from a nearby residence for further review. The estimated cost to repair the damage was provided by the victim as $119. No suspects were identified at the time, and the case was closed pending further leads.
address_block: a single-family residence in the Westside neighborhood

narrative: On December 26, 2024, at approximately 1637 hours, officers were dispatched to a retail store in the 1900 block of Park Drive, University District, regarding an armed robbery with reported injuries. The victim stated that while exiting the store and approaching their vehicle parked nearby, an unidentified male suspect wearing a dark hoodie and jeans approached the driver’s door. The suspect displayed a black handgun, pointed it at the victim, and ordered the victim out of the vehicle. The victim complied and sustained minor injuries while exiting. The suspect then entered the vehicle, taking cash and merchandise totaling approximately $13,714 before fleeing westbound on Park Drive. Officers canvassed the area for witnesses and surveillance footage. Evidence, including fingerprints and video recordings, was collected for processing. The case remains open. No arrests have been made at this time.

narrative: On April 29, 2024, at approximately 11:30 PM, officers responded to a reported credit card fraud at a retail store located in the 9400 block of Washington Drive, within the Oak Park neighborhood. Upon arrival, officers met with store management, who reported that an unknown individual had used multiple fraudulent credit cards to purchase high-value electronics and gift cards totaling an estimated loss of $77,872. Officers reviewed surveillance footage provided by the store, which showed a male suspect, approximately 30-40 years old, wearing a dark jacket and baseball cap, conducting the purchases. The suspect left the premises without incident. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers collected transaction receipts and video evidence for further investigation. The victim stated that while exiting his vehicle, he was approached by the suspect who brandished a knife and demanded his wallet and cellphone. The victim resisted, resulting in a brief struggle during which the suspect inflicted a minor injury before fleeing with the victim’s property, valued at $227. Officers canvassed the area and located the suspect nearby, matching the victim’s description (male, mid-20s, dark clothing). The suspect was placed under arrest without further incident. Officers recovered the victim’s wallet and cellphone in the suspect’s possession. Surveillance footage from a nearby storefront was secured for evidence and is under review. The victim was treated by paramedics at the scene.
address_block: the public parking lot at 9600 Hill Way

narrative: On July 2, 2024, at approximately 1542 hours, officers were dispatched to the local grocery store at 2800 Meadow Boulevard, Eastgate neighborhood, regarding a reported check fraud. Upon arrival, officers met with the store manager, who stated that an unknown individual had presented multiple fraudulent checks over the past week, resulting in a total loss of approximately $55,625. The suspect was described as a male, mid-30s, average build, wearing a dark baseball cap and blue jacket. Officers reviewed store surveillance footage, which showed the suspect cashing checks at various registers. The fraudulent checks were retained as evidence, and copies were obtained for further analysis. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Officers canvassed the area for additional witnesses, but none were located. The investigation remains open pending review of surveillance footage and further follow-up with local financial institutions.
address_block: the local grocery store located at 2800 Meadow Boulevard

narrative: On November 21, 2024, at approximately 1722 hours, officers on routine patrol in the North Hills neighborhood were flagged down by the vehicle owner at the intersection of Third Street and Washington Avenue regarding an attempted auto theft. The victim reported that upon returning to their parked vehicle, a late-model luxury sedan valued at approximately $62,898, they observed fresh tool marks around the driver’s door handle and noted that the vehicle’s alarm had been activated. The victim stated both sets of vehicle keys were in their possession at the time, suggesting the use of an electronic relay attack or similar bypass technique. Officers observed no visible damage to the ignition or windows and confirmed the vehicle remained locked and secured. A canvass of the immediate area was conducted but no additional witnesses or surveillance footage were located. The victim was provided with a case information card and advised to contact their insurance company. No injuries were reported. The suspect remains unidentified, and no arrests were made at the scene.
address_block: the intersection of Third Street and Washington Avenue

Surveillance footage was reviewed, revealing no evidence of narcotics-related activity. No injuries were reported, no arrests were made, and no weapons were involved. The investigation remains open pending additional information from witnesses or the public.

Officers collected evidence, including copies of receipts and surveillance images, and advised the victim on steps to protect their identity. The case remains under investigation. narrative: On June 6, 2023, at approximately 1:48 AM, officers were dispatched to the 5900 block of First Avenue in Midtown regarding a vehicle collision with reported injuries. The suspect was unable to recall their prior location or explain the circumstances of the incident. Paramedics treated one passenger for minor injuries at the scene. The suspect refused field sobriety tests but consented to a preliminary breath test, which registered a blood alcohol concentration of 0.15%. Officers interviewed two witnesses who reported seeing the vehicle swerve before striking a curb. Their statements were consistent and corroborated the suspect’s impaired driving. The suspect was placed under arrest for DUI causing injury. The vehicle was towed as evidence, and an investigative report was completed.

The victim, a pedestrian, reported minor injuries sustained when the suspect’s vehicle clipped their leg while parking. Standardized field sobriety tests were administered, with the suspect failing all components. A preliminary breath test indicated a BAC of 0.14%. No arrest was made at the scene pending further investigation. Officers documented injuries and collected witness statements. The case was referred to detectives for follow-up. No property loss was reported.

Officers made contact with the group and advised them of the city ordinance regarding excessive noise in public spaces. The primary suspect, described as an adult male, appeared uncooperative and refused to lower the music volume. After multiple warnings, the suspect was cited for violation of the local noise ordinance and subsequently placed under arrest for failing to comply with officers' lawful commands. No injuries were reported, and no weapons were involved. Witnesses in the area corroborated the excessive noise. The portable speaker was photographed as evidence. The case was forwarded to detectives for additional follow-up.
address_block: Westside Park near the intersection of Jefferson and Elm

narrative: On October 28, 2023, at approximately 12:11 AM, officers were dispatched to the public parking lot at 1500 Park Way in the Westside neighborhood following a report of a possible DUI involving drugs. Upon arrival, officers observed a vehicle parked askew within a designated space. The driver, later identified as an adult male, was seen exiting the driver’s seat and appeared unsteady, using the door for support and struggling to maintain balance. Officers made contact and detected a strong odor of intoxicants emanating from the subject’s breath. The subject’s speech was slurred, and his eyes were bloodshot. Standardized field sobriety tests were administered. The subject demonstrated lack of smooth pursuit during the horizontal gaze nystagmus test, failed to maintain heel-to-toe contact on the walk-and-turn, and was unable to balance during the one-leg stand. A preliminary breath test indicated a BAC of 0.13%. The subject denied recent alcohol or drug use. No injuries were reported. A canvass of the area yielded no additional witnesses. The subject was released pending further investigation. No property loss or weapons were involved.
address_block: the public parking lot at 1500 Park Way

The suspect brandished a blunt object, believed to be a tire iron, and demanded the victim exit the vehicle. Officers provided first aid and summoned EMS, who treated the victim at the scene. A canvass of the surrounding area was conducted; no additional witnesses were located. The vehicle, a silver 2018 sedan valued at $4,510, was entered into the stolen vehicle database. Officers collected surveillance footage from nearby businesses as evidence. The suspect was later located, cited, and taken into custody.

address_block: the public parking lot at 9400 Oak Way

address_block: the Starbucks coffee shop in the Greenfield Shopping Center

narrative: On December 9, 2024, at approximately 5:50 PM, officers responded to a report of criminal trespass at the Target store located at 7700 Park Boulevard in the Westside neighborhood. Upon arrival, store management identified the suspect as a male adult who had previously been formally trespassed from the premises due to prior incidents. Staff stated the suspect entered the store through the main entrance and began walking through aisles, ignoring requests to leave.
